News.title: Two dead & 19 injured after bus carrying dozens of tourists to Oktoberfest party crashes in Germany as driver detained
News.content:
BUS HORROR Two dead & 19 injured after bus carrying dozens of tourists to Oktoberfest party crashes in Germany as driver detained







Next

AT LEAST two people have died and 19 are injured after a horror bus crash in Germany.

The bus, which was on its way to Munich’s Oktoberfest beer festival, was carrying around 33 tourists when it veered off the road and overturned.

Six people were airlifted by rescue helicopter to nearby hospitals while another two were transported in ambulances.



A further 22 passengers were treated at the scene before several were also rushed to hospital.

News.title: Woman in her 70s dies in two-car smash on major A-road after Honda collides with driver going in opposite direction
News.content:
FATAL CRASH Woman in her 70s dies in two-car smash on major A-road after Honda collides with driver going in opposite direction







Next

A WOMAN has died after a horror two-car smash on a major A-road when a Honda collided with a car travelling in the opposite direction.

Emergency services raced to the A69 between Haydon Bridge and Hexham, Northumberland, just before 1.30pm yesterday.

A black Honda was travelling westbound when it crashed into a blue Volkswagen Tiguan heading the other way, cops said.

Tragically, the woman in her 70s behind the wheel of the Volkswagen was pronounced dead at the scene.





The driver of the Honda, a man in his 30s, was taken to hospital.

A section of the A69 was closed following the crash while emergency crews dealt with the scene.

The road has since reopened as cops continue to investigate the circumstances of the fatal collision.

Sergeant Greg Huntley, of Northumbria Police, said: “This is an incredibly tragic incident where a woman has lost her life.



“The thoughts of everyone here at Northumbria Police are with her loved ones.

“Our investigation is underway, and we are now appealing for further witnesses who we have not yet spoken with to come forward.

“We know this is a very busy stretch of road in Northumberland – and there will have likely been many motorists passing in both directions.

“If you were in the area or have any information that might help with our investigation, please don’t hesitate to get in touch.”

News.title: Kim Jong-un ‘tests lethal attack drone and missile swarms capable of carrying nuke warheads’ in first of its kind drills
News.content:
KIM'S WAR ARSENAL Kim Jong-un ‘tests lethal attack drone and missile swarms capable of carrying nuke warheads’ in first of its kind drills







Next

NORTH Korea has reportedly started testing lethal swarm attacks with kamikaze drones and missiles capable of carrying nuclear warheads.

The exercises have combined unmanned systems with conventional weapons, adopting tactics seen in Russia’s war against Ukraine.



Drills, which also included rocket launchers and long-range artillery, were conducted for the very first time this month, the Wall Street Journal reports.

According to North Korea’s state media, the military flex aims to hone weapon systems with a “concentrated fire” to pulverise enemy forces.



Last week Pyongyang also said it had fired a pair of hypersonic missiles.

Designed to fly at least five times the speed of sound, these state-of-the-art military weapons are capable of overcoming air defences.

The tests were overseen by North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, who said the missiles represented “ultramodern” technology.

And on Thursday, North Korean media reported test- firing shells for an updated 240mm multiple-rocket-launcher system with unmanned “pinpoint” guidance.

Swarm tactics use weapons travelling at vastly different speeds to overwhelm an opponent even with sophisticated defences.

And the tests have sparked fears that the rogue state could deploy the lethal salvo against the United States and its allies.



Supreme leader Kim has been focusing on modernising North Korea’s Soviet-era forces – while advancing the country’s nuclear weapons programme.

Collaboration with Russia has helped to quickly advance its military capability.

Since 2023, Pyongyang has ferried more than seven million artillery and mortar rounds, 100 ballistic missiles and hundreds of artillery systems into Russia, according to Ukraine’s military intelligence.



And a new road bridge linking the two war-hungry allies is “expecting more traffic”, Russian military expert Keir Giles previously told The Sun.

It comes as Moscow prepares to unleash its deadliest winter blitz yet on Kyiv, to pummel Ukraine’s defences and take the rest of Donetsk.

Earlier this month Putin said Russia’s military had been “ordered to prepare and carry out mass strikes” on Ukraine’s energy facilities.

And as Russia steps up its production of ballistic missiles – now at a rate of more than 100 a month – Kyiv’s supplies of interceptors have tumbled.

Ukraine is trying to get an additional 300 Patriot missiles from partners this winter, but there is no guarantee.



Swarm tactics have also been used by Iran this summer, forcing the US and its allies in the Middle East to burn through expensive interceptors.

Tehran has launched relentless waves of cheap missiles and drones at its enemies in a vicious bid to overwhelm air defences.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Armed clashes are increasingly determined by one side’s ability to produce missiles for multidimensional attacks faster than the other can replenish its air defences.

But a conflict involving North Korea would place even greater pressure on the US, Benjamin Jensen of the School of International Service told the WSJ.

News.title: Woman found dead with multiple stab wounds and head trauma in Central Park
News.content:
PROBE LAUNCHED Woman found dead with multiple stab wounds and head trauma in Central Park







Next

A WOMAN has been found dead in New York with multiple stab wounds and head injuries.

The body was discovered in a gazebo near Central Park’s boathouse on Sunday, police confirmed.



She was found by authorities at 9:40am with multiple slashes and trauma to the head and was pronounced dead by EMS at 10:03am.

The identity of the woman, who is believed to be in her 60s, has not been released.



An investigation is ongoing, police have said.

No arrested have been made and her cause of death is being determined by a medical examiner.



Anyone with information is urged to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

News.title: Rainbow pride flag wrapped around tourist castle sparks fury from residents as they blast: who paid for this?
News.content:
PRIDE OF DEVON Rainbow pride flag wrapped around tourist castle sparks fury from residents as they blast: who paid for this?







Next

A 500ft Pride flag wrapped around a castle has sparked a furious reaction online.

The rainbow banner was unfurled on Saturday during a four-day music and arts festival in Totnes, Devon.



One critic wrote: “Absolutely ridiculous.

“Who paid for that?



“Was it taxpayers?”

Another called the Capture the Castle ­display “disgusting”.

Local Lib Dem MP Caroline Voaden hit back, saying: “I’m so proud of the scale, diversity and quality of the Pride festival Totnes has produced, which as well as sending a clear message of equality and inclusion will also boost our local economy and growing profile as a centre for progressive arts and culture.

“We captured the castle with a huge pride flag.

“It’s so great to see Totnes buzzing with energy and fun and queer love.

“Everyone deserves to be who they are, to love who they love and to live with dignity and respect.”



Totnes Pride has previously faced questions over the use of public money for events, with the town council supporting the festival through community grant funding.

Ceri Goddard, of Totnes Pride, said the flag was loaned by Torbay Pride and English Heritage had advised on planning.

News.title: Man in his 80s dies in huge house fire after blaze destroys entire first floor of London home with woman escaping flames
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FIRE TRAGEDY Man in his 80s dies in huge house fire after blaze destroys entire first floor of London home with woman escaping flames







Next

TRAGEDY struck after an elderly man died when a fire ripped through his London home.

The man, in his 80s, was found dead after flames tore through the two-storey terraced house in Wood Green.

A woman managed to escape the property before firefighters arrived.

The devastating fire broke out in Granville Road, north London, at around 10.15pm on Saturday.





Firefighters battled to bring the flames under control, with the blaze finally extinguished by around 11.30pm.

The whole of the first floor was destroyed in the inferno, along with half of the roof.

But the horror ended in tragedy after the elderly man died at the scene.

A woman had managed to flee the burning house before crews arrived.



Cops and firefighters are now investigating what sparked the deadly blaze.

The cause of the fire remains under investigation.

A spokesman for the Met said: “Officers attended to support the London Fire Brigade and London Ambulance Service.

“Sadly, a man in his 80s died at the scene.



“His next of kin have been informed and continue to be supported.

“Specialist Met officers are currently supporting the London Fire Brigade to investigate the circumstances around the fire.”

News.title: My son didn’t come home after a night out with pals – Facebook message terrified me… then cops showed up at my door
News.content:
Next

WHEN mum Donna Roche’s 18-year-old son Lewis said “see you later” as he headed out to meet his friends one Sunday, she didn’t think for one second it would be the last thing he ever said to her.

Those were his last words, as he never came home – and tragically weeks later his body was found in a river. His death was ruled as non-suspicious, but speaking exclusively to The Sun, the heartbroken mum reveals why she fears there’s more to it.



Lewis Penfold-Roche’s remains were pulled from the River Tees near his home in Stockton on March 11 2024, six weeks after he was last seen on CCTV in a local supermarket.

His death was ruled non-suspicious, but Donna, 37, says the post mortem did not show typical signs of drowning and many of the belongings he had with him – including his coat, bag and bank cards – all remain missing.

She also claims witnesses have changed their statements, the investigation has been riddled with “lies” and she’s weighing up legal action, telling The Sun: “We don’t have any answers.”



An inquest is due to be held into the death but has been pushed back to a yet unspecified date.

“The wait has been terrible. We are still waiting for disclosure from the police,” the mum said.

“I just want anyone who knows anything to come forward. We want to know how and why Lewis ended up there.

“We won’t give up until we get answers. Getting those answers will bring us closure.”



She was also targeted by sickos who during the original search tried to scam and taunt her on Facebook.

Donna, of Stockton, County Durham, said: “They sent us messages from made up accounts saying ‘we know where he is, he’s in a caravan and he has a bag over his head’.

“They’d send us messages just to upset me. There were quite a few different ones. We also had scam messages from people saying they had information in exchange for money.

“You are not in a good state of mind and you cling to hope when you see messages like that.



“We never found out who any of them were as they were made up accounts, with no friends.

“They were horrid and they need to be dealt with. I’ve spoken to other parents who have gone through the same thing and they’ve had similar messages.”

Donna reported the messages and posts to Facebook but she claims the social media giant rejected many of her requests for action.

She added: “They said there wasn’t enough for them to take action.



“It’s ridiculous. I can put a post up and it will get taken down but these people don’t get taken down. Facebook needs to do something.”

But the wicked behaviour was not solely limited to social media.

Donna said some people also tore down missing person posters she and the rest of the community put up in her area after Lewis’ disappearance on January 28 2024.

She first reported her lad as missing on January 30 after he failed to return home.



She said: “I always play it over in my mind. He woke up in the morning, had his breakfast and said he was going to meet his friends.

“He turned around and said ‘see you later’. But there was no ‘later’, he didn’t come back. Those were his last words to me.

“It was usual for him to go out with his friends, they would go to the park and things or his friend’s house. I wasn’t worried.

“Usually he would ring or text me at night if he wanted to stay out but I had no phone call or text that night.

“My husband and I thought he might have fallen asleep and not texted. But then he didn’t come home the next day. That night I started ringing friends to see where he was.



“Everyone said they hadn’t seen him so in the morning I reported him missing to the police. The police advised me to keep calm but I had called all the local hospitals.

“I was panicking. I had no idea where he was.”

Donna said she and her sister decided to take action themselves as the police failed to find Lewis.



The pair started putting up missing posters around the area and set up a Facebook group to help find Lewis, with more than 4,000 people joining it.

Members of the group banded together to search for the teenager.

CCTV footage released during the search showed the youngster in an Esso garage in Station Road at around 8.15am. He was later seen heading down the same road at around 6pm.

But Donna said this was the final sighting of her lad.

“There was nothing after Station Road. No CCTV, doorbell footage or sightings,” she added.



She received the crushing news about Lewis’ death on March 11 2024 after she rang police for an update – something she did every day unless officers reached out to her first.

The mum-of-three said: “They told me they were at the river and then when I contacted them back they told me they were on their way to me.

“They came around and knocked on the door. All I remember is them saying sorry. I don’t remember anything after that. I was just screaming.

“I remember being on the floor and my husband holding me. The police had gone by that point.”

She later found out a woman who was walking by the river had spotted Lewis’s body and called the police.



Donna said her life was torn apart by the news.

“It’s been devastating. Every day is hard now. We wake up every morning and it’s so quiet. It’s just not the same,” she told The Sun.

Donna described her first born son as a loving, cheeky lad who enjoyed gaming and singing.

She added that Lewis, who once performed at the Royal Albert Hall with his school choir, was “loved by all”.

And the mum said the youngster’s 15-year-old brother, who is autistic, still asks after him.



She added: “He doesn’t understand why his best friend isn’t coming back. They always did things together.”

Donna is now calling on anyone who might have other information about Lewis, who was looking for work at the time of his disappearance, to reach out.

In a statement, Cleveland Police said: “The death is not being treated as suspicious hence the referral to the coroner.

“An inquest into this case will be held so we can’t comment whilst the coronial process is ongoing.”

The Sun has approached Facebook owners Meta for comment.

News.title: Two killed after car ‘travelling with another vehicle’ leaves road & crashes into lamppost – as man arrested
News.content:
CRASH TRAGEDY Two killed after car ‘travelling with another vehicle’ leaves road & crashes into lamppost – as man arrested







Next

TWO people have died after a car left the road and crashed into a lamppost – as cops make one arrest.

Emergency services descended on the scene in Rotheram, South Yorkshire shortly after 6.40pm on Saturday.

South Yorkshire Police said a white BMW 3 Series left the carriageway and crashed into a lampost on East Bawtry Road.



Despite the best efforts of emergency paramedics, fire crews and members of the public, the car’s two occupants were tragically pronounced dead at the scene.



Officers said the car had been travelling with a second vehicle before the fatal collision – a blue BMW 4 Series.

Cops have since arrested one man on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving – he has been released on police bail.

Formal identification of the victims is yet to take place, they added.

Shocking images from the scene show a heavy police presence and the road cordoned off.

Jake Richards, MP for Rother Valley, said in a statement: “I am aware of a serious incident on Bawtry road that occurred last night.

“At this stage, the respective authorities are investigating and ensuring the area is safe. My thoughts are with any victims and their families and this incredibly difficult time.

“I would urge people not to speculate at this stage as to the circumstances, but I will be contacting local authorities over the coming hours and will update the community as and when we have formal details as to what has occurred.”



A spokesperson for South Yorkshire Police said: “Officers are keen to hear from any witnesses who have not yet spoken to them, or anyone who has footage of the collision, or either vehicle prior is urged to get in touch.”

News.title: What we know about RAF base counter-terror investigation
News.content:
Gloucestershire Police said they received a call about "three suspicious vehicles" travelling towards RAF Fairford at 00:45 BST on Sunday.

Five men were later arrested by its officers near Whelford, a village around two miles (3.2km) south-east of the base.

A bomb disposal team was also deployed to the village to examine a number of vehicles, police said, around which a 400m (1,312ft) cordon is in place.

Aerial pictures showed a remote-controlled robot approaching two stationary white vans in a wooded area, though its use has not been confirmed by police.

Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) is leading the investigation into the incident.

The US military said it was "working closely" with its UK counterparts "to monitor this situation, minimise impacts and ensure the safety of US personnel, their families, and the local community".

There has been large emergency service presence in the area since the early hours of Sunday, which Gloucestershire Police Temporary Chief Constable Maggie Blyth said would remain over the next few days.

Blyth told a news conference on Sunday evening that the force would continue to assist CTP and liaise with other national partners.

She also said she would leave any declaration of a "terrorist incident" to CTP.

News.title: Burnham proposes NHS-style social care system for England
News.content:
Andy Burnham wants to offer access to free social care services to everyone in England, and will put his plans before voters at the next general election.

The prime minister told the BBC that it would be a system in which "everyone contributes, everyone is covered". He did not rule out tax rises, acknowledging it may be "difficult or unpopular" with some.

Burnham said he wants to set out his "vision" on Tuesday and Whitehall troubleshooter Baroness Casey, who is conducting a review, will advise on the "best way of doing it".

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp said the PM was suggesting Labour wanted "more tax rises" to pay for the reforms, adding the Conservatives would not support this.

Burnham has made reforming social care one of his flagship policies and has spoken of the experience of his father Roy, who had Alzheimer's and died earlier this month.

While he has been clear on his ambition to make changes to the system, he has yet to explain how any changes would be funded.

Adult social care provides state support to help people live more independently, including assistance at home.

Unlike the NHS, social care is not free at the point of use. In England and Northern Ireland, people with savings worth more than Â£23,250 are not entitled to help with care costs from their council.

In Wales and Scotland, different rules apply in terms of eligibility.

Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, the prime minister said: "I am talking about a system that works on NHS principles because that is the only way you can make it work.

"There is free personal care elsewhere in the UK. I don't think it's right that people in England don't get the same and it's not something we're going to rush."

Personal care offered in Scotland is available to all adults who are assessed as needing help with tasks including eating and bathing.

News.title: Orange Order march row goes to heart of ongoing divisions in Northern Ireland
News.content:
History shows that when the politics of Northern Ireland are wrapped up in a street dispute, friction is seldom far away.

Bitter rows in the Stormont chamber between unionists and nationalists happen almost every week, but ground-level arguments are rare these days.

The Drumcree parade dispute in Portadown is a clash of political cultures.

The Orange Order is a Protestant pro-British organisation. The area where it wants to walk is largely Catholic, and predominantly inhabited by pro-Irish nationalists.

This dispute over a piece of road is not just a local problem. It has the potential to affect other parts of Northern Ireland and the power-sharing arrangements at Stormont.

"What happens at Drumcree never stays at Drumcree," was how one retired politician put it.

News.title: Ten NHS staff removed over Noah Woods data breach
News.content:
Ten NHS staff have been removed from duty or suspended after a data breach involving the digital medical records of three-year-old Noah Woods.

Launching an "urgent" investigation, Dr Martin Mansfield, deputy chief medical officer at East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust, said that any unauthorised access of patient data was "completely unacceptable".

The trust has apologised "unreservedly" to Noah's family and said disciplinary action would be taken if needed.

A major search for Noah was carried out in the village of Brantham, Suffolk, after the child went missing on 15 September. His body was found the next day in a nearby pond by police divers.

A spokesperson for the trust said 10 employees had been "removed from active duty or suspended whilst investigations are concluded".

It comes after Sir Jim Mackey, the chief executive of NHS England, wrote to every trust on Friday, ordering stronger measures to tackle data breaches.

"We have seen too many cases of people abusing that trust, and enough is enough," said Sir Jim.

"Anyone who thinks they can satisfy their curiosity by looking at a patient's record should know this: they will be found out, they may lose their career and could end up with a criminal record."

News.title: England win series as Banton delivers on potential
News.content:
Third Metro Bank one-day international, Kia Oval

England 355-7 (50 overs): Banton 126, Brook 77, Cox 76

Sri Lanka 132 (29.1 overs): Kusal 35; Dawson 3-26

England won by 223 runs

Scorecard

Tom Banton delivered on all of his potential by crashing a brilliant first international century as England wrapped up their summer with an ODI series win over Sri Lanka.

The 27-year-old right-hander was once the rising star of English cricket when handed a debut in 2019 but afterwards fell out of love with the game after losing his way.

After reaching his hundred in 95 balls in the third one-day international at The Oval, he stood with arms wide and looked to the sky - all of that disappointment seemingly behind him.

"My fiance, Lilly, was here and all of her family," Banton said.

"Unfortunately, my mum, dad and brother weren't here because whenever my mum seems to come I don't do that well.

"Bless her, she is not banned from coming, but she avoids coming now."

The opener went on to make 126 from 105 deliveries, perfectly countering tricky early conditions - conditions in which Joe Root struggled uncharacteristically for 18 from 37 balls - and going on to share an increasingly aggressive stand of 150 in 117 balls with captain Harry Brook.

"To score a hundred for England is just the best feeling on earth," Banton said. "I don't think anything is going to beat it."

Brook made 77 and Jordan Cox, picked in the place of the injured Jos Buttler, added a 52-ball 76 to lift England to 355-7.

That always appeared a match-winning total on a surface offering bounce for the pace bowlers and turn for the spinners.

Sri Lanka crumbled to 132 all out in 29.1 overs, giving England a 223-run win and their biggest ODI victory against the tourists.

It meant England signed off their summer, one that included off-field issues, the end of Bazball, Ben Stokes' retirement and Root's surprise return as Test skipper, with a fifth successive series win amid the madness across formats.

News.title: Why Premier League faces uncertainty and chaos after Man City ruling
News.content:
If you were getting the impression that the saga over Manchester City's 115 charges was almost over, think again.

Two years and 10 days since the hearing began, and 1,329 days after City were charged, we now know a verdict has been reached, with the club guilty of the majority of financial rule breaches.

That is not because the Premier League or Manchester City have told us - it is thanks to the Athletic finding out and breaking the story., external

BBC Sport was later told the verdict was sent during the week to club executives, who had to sign a non-disclosure agreement to open the file.

A process can appear to be completely watertight, as this one certainly had been, but when the circle of trust is expanded, the chance of information getting out increases.

Despite this, public silence from the Premier League continues.

City did not address whether they had been found guilty in a statement making it clear - with an appeal expected - that the "process remains ongoing" from their point of view.

It all points to the suggestion that the long-awaited decision of the independent panel was not a case of this process nearing an end, but perhaps instead reaching the end of the beginning.

It appears the chaos and uncertainty is only going to increase now.

City fans, and the rest of football, are left to guess what the punishment might be. And when this all might reach a definitive conclusion.

The charges are so serious that some form of points deduction now appears inevitable, subject to the appeal by City, who have always insisted they have done nothing wrong.

When and how any punishment is applied will be crucial not just for City, but the Premier League as a whole.

And that's before we get to the prospect of clubs suing City for compensation.

Enzo Maresca's side go to Liverpool on 11 October when the Premier League resumes after the international break. They could go six points clear at the top. But is that now rendered meaningless?

Let's look at possible scenarios - none of which are particularly appealing.

News.title: White casts doubt on Fury-Joshua after 24 hours of chaos
News.content:
Two days after the announcement British boxing had waited a decade for, Dana White - the UFC president and Zuffa Boxing chief named as one of the figures promoting Tyson Fury against Anthony Joshua - was asked whether the fight would actually happen.

"I don't know," he said.

White was speaking at London's Copper Box on Saturday, where British heavyweight Johnny Fisher beat Michael Pirotton on his Zuffa Boxing debut. But for much of the media in attendance another heavyweight fight dominated the evening.

Asked whether Wednesday's scheduled Fury-Joshua news conference in London would take place, White added: "I have no idea."

On Thursday, Fury and Joshua were officially announced to meet at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December, live globally on Netflix. By Friday, that certainty had unravelled.

A dispute over who is entitled to promote the event led to claims of contractual breaches, talk of possible replacement fights and another flurry of cryptic social-media posts.

Even by boxing's recent standards, the past 24 hours have been extraordinary - and not a particularly flattering look for the sport.

News.title: Celebrity Traitors 2 cast: Who are this year's 'big dogs' and dark horses?
News.content:
If Carr was the star of last year's show, then perhaps his fellow TV funnymen could be the ones to watch this time around.

Naturally good readers of a room and skilled at misdirection, comedians can inject some comic relief into those tense roundtable moments.

It worked for Carr, who was considered to be less of a threat and more out of his depth by the other sleuths.

This time around, stand-up star Joe Lycett, 38, is one of the leading candidates for the role of class clown. Known for his quick wit and political stunts, Lycett told the BBC he asked Carr for advice on "how to spot a rotten little traitor like you".

Last year's winner replied: "Just anyone that's sweating and giggling."

With his brightly coloured outfits, Lycett will bring some glamour to the castle, if and when he's not donning the famous dark cloak.

"There's a lot of variety and silly stuff that I might not get to wear at all if I end up doing a Paloma," he noted, with reference to Paloma Faith, who was brutally killed off early doors last year by her supposed friend, Carr.

If laughing all the way to the winning line is to work again, then it's hard to look beyond James Acaster.

Anyone who has seen his Netflix special Repertoire or heard his podcast Off Menu will know his deadpan, absurdist humour and whimsical flights of fancy could make it difficult to tell whether he is telling the truth or not.

A "huge fan" of the show since the first non-celebrity edition in 2022, Acaster, 41, said he would prefer to be a faithful as he wasn't good at lying - though Carr did previously say something similar...

News.title: Thousands without water and roads closed after burst pipe
News.content:
Thousands of homes in parts of West Sussex have water supply issues and a number of roads have flooded after what police are describing as a "significant" leak.

Roads around the Southgate Roundabout in Crawley have been closed on Sunday morning due to the burst water pipe, Sussex Police said.

Southern Water said about 9,000 customers were impacted, but just before 18:00 BST, Crawley Borough councillor Duncan Crow said some 4,000 properties had seen seen their supplies returned.

A company spokesperson said: "Our teams are on site and working as quickly and safely as possible to repair the burst and restore supplies."

The company said customers were experiencing a loss of water supply or low pressure in the following areas - Woolborough Road, Holmcroft, Southgate, Tilgate and Furnace Green.

It first reported at 12:00 that supplies had returned to some homes.

The Southern Water spokesperson added: "Restoring water to customers as quickly as possible remains our highest priority."

John Boulton, who is 82, and his partner are without water.

He said: "It's pretty disgusting, really - we pay so much for the water supply."

Boulton said he had just paid Â£22 for bottled water in a shop.

News.title: Murder probe as cyclist dies following moped crash
News.content:
A murder inquiry has begun after an e-bike cyclist died following a collision with a moped in west London.

Emergency services were called to North Pole Road, North Kensington, at about 01:20 BST on Friday where the seriously injured 24-year-old man was found. He was pronounced dead at the scene shortly after.

Police said the investigation was at an early stage but it was believed the moped had been pursuing the e-bike cyclist prior to the crash.

Dt Ch Insp Neil John said detectives were "pursuing a number of lines of inquiry, including efforts to identify and trace the rider of the moped".

"Our thoughts are with the victim's family at what is a very difficult time," he added.

"We have launched a full investigation and are working hard to get answers and establish exactly what happened.

"As part of this, we're urging anyone who was in the area at the time and may have seen the e-bike or the moped to get in touch with us as soon as possible. If you have any information that could help, please come forward."

News.title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos
News.content:
Traitors star Paul Gorton did not think twice about sharing photographs on social media while enjoying a family holiday with his wife and two young children.

But when he returned home he discovered that his house in Cheshire had been burgled just days earlier.

"The eerie bit is at 21:10 BST I posted that me and Kate were by the side of the pool, we've got full bellies, the kids are in bed, we're actually having our little bit of the holiday," he said.

"About 20 minutes later, little did we know, our house has been broken into."

Paul's bike as well as several sentimental items including an irreplaceable ring from Kate's grandmother were stolen in the burglary on 28 August.

The perpetrators managed to break in through the bi-fold doors at the back of the house by using a technique known as lock snapping before cutting the broadband connection.

News.title: Man charged with murdering woman in Darlington
News.content:
A man has been charged with murdering a woman who was found dead by police.

Andrew Bell, 44, of Darlington, is accused of killing Leanne Park, 44, in the town on Wednesday.

Durham Police said she was pronounced dead at an address in Parkgate at about 21:15 BST. Her family said she was the "best mam, nana, daughter and friend we could wish for".

Bell is due to appear at Newton Aycliffe Magistrates' Court on Monday.

A 27-year-old man arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender has been released on bail, the force said.

A spokesperson said crime scene investigators would continue to work at the scene and a police cordon was "expected to remain in place for some time".

Anyone with information about the murder is urged to contact detectives.

News.title: Police get more time to quiz suspects in alleged plot against Jewish community
News.content:
Detectives have been granted an extra week to question two men arrested as part of an investigation into an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester.

The extension means the men - both in the 30s - can now be detained until 4 October.

The men were arrested in the Northern Quarter area of Manchester on 20 September - the eve of Yom Kippur, when thousands of British Jews were in synagogues.

A spokesperson for the Metropolitan Police, which is leading the investigation, said their work was "ongoing and officers continue to pursue a number of lines of enquiry".

News.title: 'I was angry at my husband - I didn't know he had dementia'
News.content:
Since Clive's death in 1999, Helen has been working as a dementia researcher, raising awareness of his condition and continuing his legacy through her charity, The Clive Project.

She continues to tell her story because there is still "more to be done" to help dementia patients and their families, she said.

Helen described her late-husband as a calm, level-headed and "very active guy" who used to run marathons, even "before it was popular".

"Clive was unflappable," she said.

"He reckoned he failed if he lost his temper."

But as Clive approached his 40s things began to change.

"You can't really tell at what stage somebody's behaviour changes," she said.

"Younger people in particular are always going to be difficult to diagnose.

"And he covered up some things. He never admitted to me that he was having problems with reading and writing."

While Helen had never before heard of dementia in younger people, she said she "knew there was something wrong".

"I would make plans and he would forget he was looking after the children," she said.

"We had very many arguments about it.

"He said, 'I'm just growing old' - and he was early forties then."

News.title: Your pictures of the Harvest Moon shimmering across the UK sky

The Moon reached its fullest point at 17:49 BST on Saturday but it was later, when the sky got darker, that it made its biggest impact.

News.title: Child's hidden letter found after 44 years
News.content:
A letter written by a 10-year-old girl in the 1980s and hidden in the cavity of the stairs at her home has been found 44 years later.

The house in Hockley, Essex, was undergoing renovation work when a worker found the scrap of paper and passed it to Michelle Harwood, who now lives there.

Filled with curiosity, the 36-year-old charity worker examined it - noting "really neat" handwriting for a child - and posted on her local Facebook community group on Thursday morning to track down the author.

Within an hour, multiple people had found and tagged Rachel Miles, now a 54-year- old teacher in Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire. And she responded.

News.title: Shock energy price data risks Burnham ambitions to fix social care
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Shocking new energy prices for oil and gas have provided Andy Burnham and his chancellor John Healey with a major setback as the prime minister vowed to put spending on social care at the heart of his next election manifesto.

The figures disclosed to The Independent, which the Treasury will have seen, show that oil prices are 154 per cent above the pre Iran conflict level of 77.6p per therm on 27 February. Meanwhile, gas prices are up 43 per cent since the war began.

Treasury sources have noted that higher energy prices feed inflation and hike borrowing costs, but while that can temporarily increase tax revenue it weakens the economy.

It causes a huge headache as Mr Healey tries to balance the books with uncertainty as well as a push to increase defence spending to 3 per cent of GDP.

The figures highlight the massive constraint on Mr Healey’s Budget, due to be unveiled at the end of October, as he prepares to address the Labour Party conference for the first time as chancellor on Tuesday with a desire to reindustrialise Britain.

It comes as Mr Burnham played his highest stakes yet as prime minister on Sunday when he vowed that he would put his plan for a national care service along the lines of the NHS, funded by the taxpayer and free at the point of use, to the public at the next general election.

With no clear plan to pay for it or his other promises on taking VAT off energy bills and capping bus fares, the issue could dominate the next election campaign and see any hopes of cross party consensus collapse.

Speaking on the eve of conference, the prime minister had acknowledged he was facing a “challenging” set of circumstances against severe economic headwinds, adding it was “crucial” to stabilise public finances to fulfil his plans. Then on Sunday, he said he would “grasp the nettle” of social care reform in England, saying it is “devastating” that generations of politicians had failed to address the crisis in the system.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham said he would put his plan for a national care service along the lines of the NHS, funded by the taxpayer and free at the point of use, to the public at the next general election ( PA )

Mr Burnham warned that Sir Keir Starmer’s red lines on tax – no increases in national insurance, income tax or VAT – constrained him from fixing the “broken” social care system before another election.

But the growing international and economic uncertainty puts his plans at risk with energy set to become a major factor in his government’s calculations.

The revelation that social care would be at the centre of the election manifesto came as Labour’s annual conference in Liverpool opened with the slogan “hope again”, reflecting the dramatic change the party underwent in replacing their election-winning prime minister with Mr Burnham.

Mr Burnham came into office in July, weeks after winning the Makerfield by-election, and ending his time as mayor of Greater Manchester, saying that he did not want to leave Downing Street without fixing a crisis that has become very personal to him because of the plight of his father who suffered from Alzheimer’s before dying earlier this month.

But now, despite an offer to work cross-party on the issue, he risks an election defeat before he can enact change.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham (left) and John Healey on the new Royal Daffodil Ferry ( PA )

However, Mr Burnham denounced the current social care system as “unfair as American healthcare, where the most vulnerable in society can lose everything”, as he warned it will “in the end, break the National Health Service”.

Mr Burnham said the proposed care service will “work on NHS principles” but said it will not be introduced before the next election.

He told the BBC that current commitments in the Labour manifesto – which includes a pledge not to raise VAT, income tax, or national insurance – would “make it hard to do in this parliament”.

He said he “will develop a very clear plan, and I will put that plan to the public at a general election”.

“That will be that will be where the plan gets tested. And people will then be able to decide,” Mr Burnham continued. “And I am prepared to put myself in that position, recognising that it might be difficult or unpopular with some, but that is the way to do it, to get that endorsement and then introduce the system in the next parliament.”

He said that launching a national social care service along NHS principles is “the only way that you can make it work”.

open image in gallery Labour’s conference in Liverpool began on Sunday with the slogan ‘hope again’ ( Getty )

“To be honest with you, broken social care will, in the end, break the national health service if we leave it like it is,” he said.

He also branded social care in England as “unfair as American healthcare” where vulnerable people can be “wiped out, not just by the condition that they have, but wiped out financially”.

He rejected suggestions a free care service could cost taxpayers £18bn a year, telling the BBC: “It’s not that high.”

But he said people were already paying a high cost for the current system: “People are paying care charges now. They are spending tens of thousands of pounds from their savings, sometimes losing their homes.

“That is what’s happening at the moment. So to suggest there isn’t a cost to people at this moment in time, there’s a huge cost.”

Labour’s conference in Liverpool began on Sunday, with the party’s deputy leader Lucy Powell and first secretary Louise Haigh addressing members from the podium.

open image in gallery Mr Burnham with first secretary of state Louise Haigh after her speech on Sunday ( PA )

The prime minister will make his speech, aimed at outlining his broad agenda for government, on Tuesday, telling Ms Kuenssberg that many of the answers people have on taxation and the economy will be given then.

He said he would lay out the “vision” for his social care plans in his speech, before Baroness Louise Casey’s review helps “work up the details”.

“Is there any wonder that politics is in such low esteem with the public when it can’t fix something as basic as the care that we give to each other?” he said.

“So it can’t carry on. Somebody needs to grasp the nettle. I will be the one to do that and I realise it might require me to spend some political capital. That it might make me unpopular with some, but that isn’t going to stop me.”

The conference opened with renewed hope in the Labour Party over its prospects of defeating Reform and the Tories after a period of dire unpopularity under Sir Keir.

An eve of conference Opinium poll put the party four points ahead of Reform with their highest percentage since 2024 of 28 per cent.

News.title: Alyssa Thompson strikes as Chelsea see off Arsenal in derby
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Chelsea beat London rivals Arsenal 1-0 at Stamford Bridge to move up to third in the Women’s Super League.

The Blues went ahead six minutes before half-time when the visitors were caught playing out from the back and Alyssa Thompson slotted in after Keira Walsh’s shot had been saved.

The Gunners – who had drawn their last two WSL matches – improved in the second half, with Chloe Kelly’s angled drive blocked and Alessia Russo’s shot charged down, but the hosts saw out the closing stages for a third WSL win.

open image in gallery Alyssa Thompson of Chelsea celebrates scoring her team’s first goal with teammate Melvine Malard ( Getty )

Chelsea are level on 10 points with Tottenham, who had earlier thrashed Aston Villa 4-0, with Victoria Pelova scoring twice at the BetWright Stadium.

Netherlands midfielder Pelova – signed after leaving Arsenal in the summer – broke the deadlock in the 54th minute and then fired in a second off the underside of the crossbar for a fourth goal in two WSL games.

Spurs – who thrashed promoted Crystal Palace 7-0 last week – sealed victory after Caitlin Dijkstra headed in and Cathinka Tandberg added a fourth with two minutes left.

open image in gallery Victoria Pelova of Tottenham Hotspur celebrates scoring ( Getty )

Beata Olsson’s early header and Cornelia Kapocs’ late goal earned the bragging rights for Liverpool in a 2-0 Merseyside derby victory over Everton at Anfield.

Manchester United secured their first WSL victory under new boss Eva Olid with a 2-1 win over West Ham in Leigh, after goals from Elisabeth Terland and summer signing Andrea Medina. Viviane Asseyi scored a consolation for the Hammers from the penalty spot in added time.

Birmingham drew 3-3 with Crystal Palace at St Andrew’s – where Oceane Hurtre had fired the Blues ahead after 40 seconds for the quickest goal of the WSL season so far.

News.title: RAF Fairford: Terror police ‘investigate Iran link’ to suspected bomb plot near airbase
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Five men detained near an RAF base used by the US have been arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.

A major incident was declared and 85 homes evacuated near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire after several men were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences Sunday morning.

Counter Terrorism Policing detectives leading the response are said to be investigating whether the alleged plot is linked to Iran, according to The Times.

Detectives are reported to be keeping an open mind but one line of inquiry is likely to be whether the incident is linked to Tehran because the base hosts the United States Air Force (USAF) and has been used to launch operations against Iran.

US President Donald Trump claimed the alleged plot was “looking to do big damage” as he praised the joint operation with UK law enforcement.

“We had them under investigation,” he told reporters in the US. “They, they were looking to do big damage to our fort, and working with the British worked out great.”

open image in gallery Police at a road block near RAF Fairford (Ben Birchall/PA) ( PA Wire )

Four USAF bombers landed at RAF Fairford this spring after then-prime minister Sir Keir Starmer granted permission for “defensive” US action against Iranian missile sites from UK bases.

In July, the British government insisted it “stands ready 24/7 to defend itself” after Iran said UK airbases used by the US were considered “legitimate targets”.

Aerial footage from the scene in the village of Welford, near the base, showed a British Army bomb disposal squad using specialist robotic equipment to examine three white vans.

A force spokesperson said: “At around 12.45am today, police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards the air base.

“Armed officers responded and five men were arrested in the Whelford area on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. They were further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act, contrary to section 5 of the Terrorism Act.”

Investigators will be working to analyse any devices seized from those arrested to establish details of any plot and any potential motivation.

open image in gallery Counter terror police are leading the investigation ( PA )

Fairford has been raised to the highest threat level, Delta, while US airbase Lakenheath in Suffolk is on Charlie alert, the second-highest threat level that can be issued by the US Department of Defense.

The police operation near the village of Whelford in Gloucestershire was not intelligence-led, meaning investigators had not known about any potential plot in advance.

Julian Tudsbery, who has lived in Whelford for 30 years, said a resident had reported three “suspicious vans” in the village in the early hours of Sunday morning.

“Evidently, they phoned the airbase police, who didn’t answer the phone,” he said. “It just rang out so she dialled 999.”

He said he was evacuated at around 7am, adding: “(The police) were then banging on the door, so I went downstairs in my dressing gown.

“There were several police, three police cars in the drive, and they said you need to evacuate, there’s been a major incident, said he couldn’t elaborate.”

A 400m cordon has been put in place around the vehicles while villagers were evacuated to a nearby leisure centre.

A large emergency services presence was seen in the area, including a Hazardous Area Response Team, the fire service and local police.

open image in gallery A US Air Force B-1 Lancer bomber is pictured on the tarmac at RAF Fairford ( AFP/Getty )

Gloucestershire Police said: “A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident.

“It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act. The Army’s specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles.

“The local residents are being evacuated to a nearby leisure centre. A cordon is currently in place but we’d like to reassure people that we believe this incident is contained.

“We are working closely with our partners and are enacting the well-rehearsed plans we have in place.”

A spokesperson for the US Air Force said its personnel based at RAF Fairford “remain vigilant”.

“For operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures,” the spokesperson added.

“The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families.

“We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families.”

open image in gallery Fire crews are at the scene after a major incident was declared in Fairford ( Reuters )

Security measures at the site in southwest England have significantly increased with roadblocks and armed police preventing access and emergency vehicles parked nearby, Reuters reported on Sunday.

The airbase also hosts the annual Royal International Air Tattoo (RIAT), though this year’s event in May was cancelled because of the military operations.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, currently attending the annual Labour Party conference in Liverpool, is receiving updates on the situation.

A government spokesperson added: “We are grateful to the emergency services, who have acted quickly to detain several suspects and put measures in place to keep the community safe.

“It would be inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing.”

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting confirmed the incident is “being dealt with” and thanked the emergency teams who acted “so swiftly”.

“It is exactly why our emergency response teams and Armed Forces are on standby 24/7,” he added.

A woman living on the base’s perimeter described an apparent increase in military security in recent weeks.

open image in gallery RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk has also been put on high alert ( Reuters )

The woman, who asked not to be identified, told the Press Association: “In the prior few weeks they have put heavy, very heavy, vehicles across all gates.”

She described them as “very big tractors and things like that” parked behind crash-gates into the base, adding: “So obviously they’re taking security seriously”.

“Great big concrete walls” have also been placed behind some gates, including on Dunfield Loop and Whelford Road, the resident, who has lived there for about 50 years, told the press association.

The arrests come amid heightened concerns around the threat from hostile states to the UK, with Russia and Iran among those that have used proxies to commit crimes on their behalf on British soil.

News.title: ‘Stupid on stilts’: Republican senator blasts Donald Trump Jr for wedding party funded by Putin ally and believes it could impact midterms
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Republican Senator Thom Tillis has slammed Donald Trump Jr.’s Caribbean wedding party, bankrolled by a Russian oligarch with ties to Vladimir Putin, as “stupid on stilts.”

He is one of a growing number of Republicans calling for an investigation into Trump Jr after Putin ally Umar Kremlev paid for celebrations when he married socialite Bettina Anderson in the Bahamas in May.

Tillis, who is retiring when his term ends in January, told CNN’s State of the Union Sunday that he would leave it to the Judiciary Committee chairs to decide whether or not to subpoena the president’s son, before laying into the absurdity of the situation.

“Folks, this was stupid on stilts,” Tillis, of North Carolina, said. “You’d think somebody would’ve gotten a memo of a bad look.”

“To have a Russian oligarch who’s actually traveled in a delegation to Beijing fund some sort of island wedding for a very wealthy family that also happens to be related to the president? Come on, guys, this is amateur hour,” Tillis said.

open image in gallery ‘To have a Russian oligarch who’s actually traveled in a delegation to Beijing fund some sort of island wedding for a very wealthy family that also happens to be related to the president? Come on, guys, this is amateur hour,’ Tillis said. ( CNN )

The North Carolina senator noted the scandal unfolded “at a time when we need our pros on the field.”

“We got an election to win in 37 days. How this helps…I can’t imagine,” he said.

He added: “Maybe Don Jr. can give us a reasonable example why tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars from an oligarch went into a wedding in some beach location, but boy, I’d sure like to see the rationale behind it. On its face, it doesn't look very smart.”

Kremlev, head of the International Boxing Association, helped pay for a private island and fireworks show during Trump Jr.’s wedding celebrations, according to records reviewed by ProPublica.

On Instagram, Bettina Trump wrote that Kremlev was a “dear friend” who “very generously hosted two incredible nights of celebrations for us AFTER our wedding.”

open image in gallery Donald Trump Jr. and his wife Bettina Anderson had some of their May wedding paid for by an ally of Russian president Vladimir Putin ( Getty )

President Donald Trump defended the wedding being partially bankrolled by the Russian oligarch, telling reporters on September 18: “It’s totally allowed.” He added that he believed his son was paying them back.

Within days, members of Trump’s own party were calling for an investigation into whether Trump Jr. used his proximity to his father for financial benefit regarding the wedding.

Republican Senator John Curtis of Utah called on the Senate Judiciary Committee to subpoena Trump Jr. over his business dealings, relationship with foreign entities and gifts or other benefits he has received as a result of being the president’s son.

Curtis, in a letter sent last week to the Senate Judiciary Committee last Tuesday, said Trump Jr. should face the same scrutiny that Hunter Biden, the son of former President Joe Biden, a Democrat, has, and suggested that both men should answer questions about whether they used their family connections to turn a profit.

open image in gallery Senator John Curtis is asking the Senate Judiciary Committee to investigate presidential family members, including a report that a Russian oligarch helped pay for the wedding party of Donald Trump Jr. ( Getty )

“For years, serious questions have been raised about members of presidential families using their names and proximity to the President to advance private business interests,” Curtis wrote in a letter to the committee.

He asked that an investigation be launched into “the use of presidential family relationships for private financial benefit, preferential treatment, or access by domestic and foreign interests.”

Two Republicans on the Judiciary panel, Tillis and Texas Senator John Cornyn, also said they would support an investigation. Tillis is retiring this year and Cornyn lost his seat in a primary earlier this year to a Trump-backed opponent.

Another Republican, Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, said she was glad Curtis sent the letter.

“It doesn’t make any difference if you’re Republican or Democrat, if you’re Trump or you’re Biden,” she said.

With reporting by the Associated Press

News.title: 3 killed and 4 injured in mass shooting at ‘after-hours’ spot in Detroit

Three people died and four more are injured after a mass shooting at an “after-hours” spot in Detroit on Sunday, according to police.

Cops got a ShotSpotter notification about the shooting before a 911 call came just before 7:30 a.m. Police arrived at the scene within four minutes and found three men who had been fatally shot, Detroit Police Chief Todd Bettison told reporters at a news conference.

Four more people – two men and two women – were taken to nearby hospitals in private cars. All the victims are thought to be in their 20s and 30s, Bettison said.

“A fight occurred, an altercation occurred, and as a result individuals decided to settle it with gun violence,” he said.

“This address is not new to the Detroit Police Department,” he said, noting police had seven calls to the location this year. He said the department had leads but wouldn’t discuss them any further.

“This was an after-hours location,” he said of the shooting scene. “Imagine a strip club. … I'll leave it at that.”

"Regardless of what was occurring in this particular location, no one deserves to have their life ended or to be wounded by gun violence," Bettison added.

Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield urged anyone with information to contact authorities.

“We know that we need more people to speak up to bring justice to the situation,” she said at the news conference. “It’s heartbreaking and our community should not suffer from this type of violence.”

News.title: Tom Banton reflects on ‘best feeling on earth’ after his first England century
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Tom Banton described his first England century as “the best feeling on earth” – even though his mother played her part by staying away.

Banton’s superb 126 from 105 balls was the headline performance in a thumping 223-run win over Sri Lanka, as the hosts wrapped their international summer with a 2-1 success in the Metro Bank ODI Series.

The Somerset batter’s coming-of-age knock has been a long time coming. He first pulled on an England shirt in 2019 but endured a lengthy spell in the wilderness after his form nosedived.

Handed a second chance last summer, he has gradually found his feet in the set-up and finally took his turn in the spotlight with a match-winning knock at the Kia Oval.

open image in gallery Tom Banton enjoyed a day to remember (Nigel French/PA) ( PA Wire )

His parents Jayne and Colin were not in the stands to watch him soak up the acclaim but the 27-year-old revealed that was not entirely by accident.

“My fiancee Lily was here, and all of her family. Unfortunately my mum, dad and brother were not here because whenever my Mum comes I don’t seem to go that well!” he explained.

“Bless her…she’s not banned but I think avoids coming now. It would have been awesome if they were here, but unfortunately they weren’t.

“To score a hundred for England is the best feeling on earth, I don’t think anything is going to beat it.

“To finally get over the line was a feeling I couldn’t really explain to anyone. It’s been an amazing day.”

Banton’s crowning moment came in his 53rd appearance in the Three Lions, 43 of which have come in T20s, and would not have happened without Jacob Bethell’s knee injury creating a temporary vacancy at opener.

“I’m sure there were times when you’re sat there in your room thinking ‘will the chance ever come again’,” he said.

“I couldn’t be more grateful to Brooky and Baz (Harry Brook and Brendon McCullum) for giving me an opportunity again.”

Banton’s contribution, combined with an eye-catching 76 from Jordan Cox in his first one-dayer for almost two years, gave England plenty of cause for optimism about their bench strength.

Despite missing first-choice players Jos Buttler, Adil Rashid, Sam Curran and Bethell through injury, they turned in one of their most emphatic performances of the year. As well as piling 355 for seven, they were ruthless with the ball as they floored the tourists for 132 in less than 30 overs, including three wickets for Liam Dawson.

“I thought that was a near-perfect performance there,” said captain Harry Brook, who made 77.

“I thought everyone chipped in and it was an exceptional win. There were some tough periods but I thought the patience we showed was exceptional. That is the side we want to be: we want to win when they are not in our favour and when they are. We want to nail sides.

“We are building towards a squad where someone can come into a role and fill it exceptionally well. We are building a strong squad and I have full trust in anyone who comes in.”

What is RAF Fairford?

RAF Fairford, located on the border of Gloucestershire and Wiltshire, is also used by the United States Air Force (USAF).

The arrests also come amid heightened concerns around the threat from hostile states to the UK, with Russia and Iran among those that have used proxies to commit crimes on their behalf on British soil.

What have police chiefs said?

At around 12.45am on Sunday, police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards the air base.

Armed officers arrested five suspects in the Whelford area on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. They were further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act, contrary to section 5 of the Terrorism Act.

open image in gallery A plane on the ground at RAF Fairford amid the security alert ( PA Wire )

Counter Terrorism Policing senior national coordinator, Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans said: “We are in the early stages of an investigation, and five men remain in custody. As you would expect we are working closely with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident.

“We continue to work with Gloucestershire Police to keep the community safe as we work to gather evidence from the scene. A 400m cordon has been put in place around the vehicles while the Army’s Explosive Ordinance Disposal unit conduct examinations. As a precaution, around 85 households have been evacuated whilst these examinations take place.”

Gloucestershire Police said they have “well-rehearsed plans” for dealing with major incidents.

open image in gallery Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone of Gloucestershire Police said they have 'well-rehearsed plans' for major incidents ( Reuters )

A Met Police spokesperson added on Sunday afternoon: “Counter Terrorism Policing can now confirm they are leading an investigation into an incident which took place overnight near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire.

“At around 12.45am today (Sunday 27 September), police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards the air base.

“Armed officers responded and five men were arrested in the Whelford area on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. They were further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act, contrary to section 5 of the Terrorism Act.”

News.title: Five reasons why Australia’s win over Boks was an all-time classic
News.content:
If the Wallabies play like this in their own backyard at their own World Cup next year, boy we are in for a treat. After years in the doldrums, this five-try victory over South Africa was the latest reminder of their transformation under the stewardship of Les Kiss.

Their gritty performance in Perth – the city where Australia will open rugby’s showpiece in 12 months’ time – was caveated by the fact they were facing a second-string Boks side. But there can be no denying they are on an upward trajectory, even if their discipline dramatically deserted them late on.

In a helter-skelter denouement, Australia played the majority of the final 10 minutes of the match with 11 men on the pitch as South Africa threatened to mount a late comeback. Tom Wright’s eye-catching intercept try looked to have secured a match-winning moment, but it was scratched off after Hunter Paisami joined Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan and Joseph Sua’ali’i in the bin.

Ox Nche’s 80th-minute score made it a four-point game with time left for the restart, but Australia had enough fight to secure a dramatic victory largely built on execution and patience.

Five tries by the hour mark, including a Len Ikitau first-half double, ultimately gave South Africa a mountain to climb. The Wallabies’ field coverage and industriousness in defence was far superior to that of the four-time world champions, while Max Jorgensen and Sua’ali’i were pillars of excellence out wide.

After clinching a 3-1 win over New Zealand in their historic “Greatest Rivalry” series, Rassie Erasmus had the luxury of resting several of his A-listers for this one-off Test in Western Australia. The changes ultimately had an adverse effect, with the visitors faulty at the set-piece and lacking their usual snarl and bite. They found themselves playing catch-up in a chaotic game that Australia, despite their discipline creaking in the dying moments, deserved to win.

Here, Telegraph Sport explores five reasons why this was one of the craziest Test matches in recent memory.

Wallabies outmuscle Boks over 60 emphatic minutes

The Wallabies front up impressively to earn a seven-point lead at the break after a quickfire Len Ikitau double cancels out tries from Johan Grobbelaar and Edwill van der Merwe, before Ben Donaldson finishes a sublime attacking set from the hosts.

News.title: England show ODI depth in thrashing of Sri Lanka
News.content:
England’s international summer comes to an end at the Oval with a series decider against Sri Lanka. After England won the first game in Durham, Sri Lanka bounced back to take a 16-run win at Headingley on Thursday to set up this winner-takes-all match today. Sri Lanka put up a much better fight in the second one-day international than they have throughout the rest of their white-ball tour. The tourists posted 321 for six, with their captain Kusal Mendis leading the way with 121 off 100 balls, his seventh ODI century.

England’s reply got off to the best possible start, with both openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett hitting fifties. It appeared to be going well for England, with Jos Buttler and Will Jacks also registering half centuries, but Buttler’s hamstring injury in addition to the regular loss of wickets meant Sri Lanka were able to claim victory to take us to a series decider in London today.

“I am so happy winning and getting the hundred,” Mendis said. “The overall performance was very good. We started really well and the middle order batted really well. Nothing special, basic cricket and I was very happy with 320, we wanted more than 300 on this pitch. [Dunith] Wellalage bowled really well, the whole team, after the powerplay. The guys gave 100 per cent. Today [Thursday] is finished and now we have to focus on the next game and do the basics right.”

When Buttler retired hurt in the 38th over of England’s run chase, the hosts were 254 for four and were in a great position to chase the total down and claim a series victory. From the 37th over onwards, England were only able to score one four and one six.

“It was an outstanding game,” England captain Harry Brook said. “You can look back and dwell on some many different areas but that is not what this team does, we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the Oval. We put up a really good fight with the ball. To restrict them to 320 and have the chance to chase that down was a hell of an effort.

“The lads got the chase off to a flyer. You could not really ask for much more. We probably stalled in that middle period and lost a few too many wickets, but the fight we showed was great. We have got a great opportunity now to try and win this series, and a great opportunity for 12 months’ time. In pressure situations, like the one that awaits us at the Oval, it will be great to see where we are as a team.”

Buttler has been ruled out of this match due to a hamstring injury and has been replaced in the squad by Dan Lawrence, who had been playing for Surrey in the final round of the County Championship.

Play from the Oval will get under way at 10.30am.

News.title: Saracens storm Leicester to launch new Venter era in style
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Gallagher Prem meeting as Leicester Tigers host Saracens at Welford Road.

Last season, Leicester reached the play-off semi-finals in Geoff Parling’s first full season at the club, before losing to arch-rivals Northampton Saints, who went on to win their third title in the competition.

In a new era for Leicester as they plot a route back to the very top, Aaron Wainwright and Mako Vunipola make their Prem debuts.

Leicester head coach Geoff Parling is brimming with excitement ahead of this tasty match and has talked about his side’s preparation for the new season.

“Firstly we are looking to evolve our game, we’re not looking to rip it up and completely restart,” he said. This team is built on being competitive and winning, we’ve got to be in the mix every year. For me it’s all about being consistently near the top and then getting in those big games and having the ability to perform in them.”

“I’m well aware that there’s lots of elements from the season and different circumstances but the main thing is that the league is designed to have a top four that go into the play-offs so the top four is the aim.”

Saracens finished one place below Leicester in the previous campaign and missed out on the play-offs after a 32-12 final round loss to Exeter Chiefs.

Boss Joe Shaw has handed debuts to Tomos Williams and Alfie Barbeary, and he’s raring to go ahead of this fixture.

“We’ve had a great pre-season, but we’re itching to get stuck into the league campaign now,” he said. “We have a really competitive squad who are driving standards and good habits across the pitch. We are confident in the squad we have put together and are excited to see what they can achieve this campaign.”

Kick-off is at 15:00.

News.title: England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation
News.content:
Tuchel does not plan to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.
