Few balls have been so widely derided as the one created for the 2010 World Cup, where its unpredictable flight saw it denounced as uncontrollable. Yet 16 years later, the demands of the world’s best footgolfers mean anyone in possession of a Jabulani is now sitting on a goldmine, with boxed models going for upwards of £500 and the value only increasing.

“It’s a bit mad,” admits Hertfordshire-based Clarke, who has topped the footgolf world rankings five times. “No one could control the ball in the [2010] World Cup, but here we are using it for a precision sport. We all trust it and rely on it. It’s very strange.”

View image in fullscreen The Adidas Jabulani ball proved unpopular at the 2010 World Cup but is coveted by footgolfers. Photograph: Alicia Canter/The Guardian

The reason lies in the Jabulani’s precise engineering defect that so frustrated footballers on the biggest stage. Constructed from eight thermally bonded panels – a decrease from the 14 in its 2006 World Cup Adidas Teamgeist predecessor – the Jabulani reduced seams to a bare minimum, creating the smoothest, roundest ball ever made.

When struck with minimal spin at the high speeds that top-level footballers tend to shoot or cross, it caused a chaotic knuckle-ball effect, generating sudden swerves or dips. Conversely, for footgolfers, who hit a ball with the inside of their foot to generate consistent spin, the Jabulani’s reduced seams help it travel further than any other ball. Only Adidas’ offshoots from the same era – including the Teamgeist, Terrapass, Speedcell and original Torfabrik – come close.

With none of these models in production for close to 15 years, elite footgolf’s demand has coupled with a scarcity in supply to send prices soaring.

View image in fullscreen Ben Clarke has not bought a Jabulani for years due to cost. Photograph: Alicia Canter/The Guardian

“They are getting rarer and more expensive,” says Clarke, who has three boxed Jabulanis, alongside a host of other Adidas balls from that era. “I haven’t bought one for a few years, just because of how expensive they are. You tend to get them off other footgolfers or collectors who sell them because they see the footgolf market.

“The last one I got was around £250 about three years ago, but they are now £500 or more. It can be an expensive mistake if you kick it into a tree and it bursts.”

There is a consensus within the sport that the situation is unsustainable. Sean Rontree, a director of footgolf’s governing body in England, has three Jabulanis and three Speedcells in his own personal collection. He foresees an imminent end point.

“There will come a time when there won’t be any more on the market,” says Rontree. “Adidas won’t entertain making any more. We’ve had conversations with them, but the numbers they would have to ask for to make it profitable – around 10,000 balls – were out of our reach.”

The shortage has sparked an arms race. Targeting the 1,200 players who competed in this summer’s Footgolf World Cup in Mexico, a host of entrepreneurs are attempting to create a bespoke ball that can achieve the holy grail of challenging the Jabulani. Brands including the FGB (Malaysia), Squb (the Netherlands), Triero (Britain) and Birdie (Brazil) have all released footgolf-specific balls that retail for about £100.

View image in fullscreen Ben Clarke: ‘The world of footgolf and balls is ridiculous.’ Photograph: Alicia Canter/The Guardian

“I think, overall, our ball is superior in terms of quality and not needing repairs,” says FGB founder Jeffrey Cottam, whose company are now on their third-generation ball. “But in terms of trying to beat the Jabu, I don’t think anyone is there yet.

“The hardest bit is distance. Our ball is maybe five, six, seven metres behind the Jabu. We want to replicate the bounce of the Jabu, because that thing continuously bounces down the fairway. I’m trying to bring out a ball next year that beats the Jabu in all departments. There has to be a ball that comes out which is just as competitive as it. It’s the natural course of things.”

Clarke remains pragmatic. He knows the sport cannot survive for ever on a finite, decaying stock. But until a true heir emerges, he will continue his monthly ritual of tending to his dwindling Jabulani flock.

“It’s bizarre what we have to do to extend the life of a ball, just so it’s there when we need it,” he says. “One of them gave up on me last week and started chucking air out of one of the panels, so maybe I didn’t pump it up enough. The world of footgolf and balls is ridiculous.”

Sports.title: Liverpool and Manchester United handed further injury blows as star duo are forced off
Sports.content:
Liverpool and Manchester United handed further injury blows as star duo are forced off

Liverpool and Manchester United's injury woes could be set to intensify after Sunday's Nations League action.

Both Cody Gakpo and Patrick Dorgu were forced off during the first half of their nations' respective matches.

3 Gakpo is the latest Liverpool player to suffer an injury on international duty Credit: Getty

Gakpo was taken off just 17 minutes into the Netherlands' clash with Serbia.

It comes after Alexander Isak left the Sweden camp to return to Merseyside early due to an injury.

The Reds have confirmed the striker will be assessed by the club's medical staff after scoring against Romania on Friday.

How did Cody Gakpo suffer his injury?

Fans will be hoping Gakpo will not be joining Isak on the treatment table in the coming days.

However, they face a nervy wait to discover the severity of the injury which ended his night early against Serbia.

Gakpo was on the end of a strong challenge from Sasa Lukic in the centre of the park just 12 minutes into the match in Belgrade.

Despite initially staying down after the foul, he appeared as if he would be able to continue, only to signal to the bench that he would have to come off moments later.

The 27-year-old was subsequently replaced by Ruben van Bommel in the 17th minute.

It did not appear to affect Xavi's side, though, as they took the lead through a Mexx Meerdink penalty before half-time.

Gakpo has two goals and four assists in six appearances across all competitions so far this season for Liverpool.

3 Gakpo was forced off following a heavy challenge from Lukic during the Netherlands' clash with Serbia Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Andoni Iraola's side return to action at home to Manchester City on Sunday, October 11.

The Reds boss is already without long-term absentees Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike and Conor Bradley.

How did Patrick Dorgu pick up his injury?

As for United, they face similar concerns over Dorgu after he lasted just over half an hour for Denmark against Wales.

The versatile full-back headed straight down the tunnel after limping off in the 31st minute to be replaced by Mohamed Daramy.

Dorgu's injury follows the news that Bruno Fernandes will miss Portugal's match on Sunday.

The Red Devils captain has been ruled out of his country's trip to Norway due to injury.

3 United also now face an anxious wait over the fitness of Dorgu Credit: Getty

Fernandes also missed training on Saturday having been taken off late on against Wales on Thursday.

However, he remains with the squad and has not been ruled out of their final two matches of the international break.

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool striker gets stand named after him at World Cup stadium
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool striker gets stand named after him at World Cup stadium

Celta Vigo have renamed a stand after club legend Iago Aspas ahead of hosting matches at the 2030 World Cup.

The former Liverpool striker will also be honoured with a statue outside the entrance to the stadium.

3 Celta have renamed the Tribuna stand after all-time top scorer Aspas Credit: Getty

Aspas is Celta's all-time leading scorer and appearance maker having returned to his boyhood club for a second spell in 2015.

How many goals has Iago Aspas scored for Celta Vigo?

Either side of a disappointing two years at Anfield, the 39-year-old has scored 223 goals in 578 appearances for the club.

In contrast, the ex-Spain international scored just once in 15 matches for Liverpool between 2013 and 2015.

The veteran forward signed a new one-year deal with Celta in May through to the end of this season.

His legacy has now been immortalised in the stands as well as outside Bailados.

The club are have renamed the Tribuna stand after Aspas as part of their redevelopment project.

Their home since 1928 is currently being expanded ahead of the 2030 World Cup.

Once completed, the capacity will increase from 24,870 to more than 40,000 fans.

Ongoing work on the Gol stand had caused fans to speculate it would be the section named after Aspas.

A total of 7,000 new seats will be installed once it fully reopens in January, with the partially open stand currently holding just 800 supporters.

3 Aspas will also be honoured with a statue outside the entrance to Balaidos Credit: Getty

However, Aspas' name will instead adorn the Tribuna, which has been renamed the Iago Aspas Tribuna.

Mayor of Vigo Abel Caballero confirmed the decision in a video announcement as he responded to the online speculation.

Caballero explained: "Why the Tribuna stand? First, because it is already operational and, therefore, the name is immediate.

"Second, because it will be the stand with the largest capacity in Balaídos.

"And third, very importantly, because next to the Tribuna stand will be the sculpture that the City Council is going to install for Iago Aspas, right there in front."

He added: "Therefore, everything fits. So the Tribuna stand will immediately be called the Iago Aspas Tribuna stand, because it is already operational."

3 Celta's Balaidos will have its capacity increased to more than 40,000 ahead of the 2030 World Cup Credit: Getty

Celta's stadium renovation

Whilst the renovations began last year, work on the Tribuna is not set to begin until later in the season.

The stand will be reconstructed, with its capacity increasing from 5,500 seats to 16,000.

It will also be moved backwards to accommodate the additional seating.

Balaidos has been selected as one of 20 stadiums to be used in Spain, Morocco and Portugal for the 2030 World Cup.

The three nations will co-host the tournament alongside opening matches in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay to mark the World Cup's centenary.

Celta's ground previously hosted matches during the 1982 edition of the tournament, which marks the last time Spain served as hosts.

Sports.title: Calls to strip Man City of Premier League titles as ex-club chairman wants ‘terminal’ punishment
Sports.content:
Manchester City face a 'hammering' after being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules.

That's the view of talkSPORT's Henry Winter, who has also called for Man City to be stripped of the three Premier League titles they won during the period in which they were found to be in breach of the rules.

2 It's been suggested City should be stripped of three Premier League titles, including their first under Pep Guardiola in 2017/18 Credit: Getty

City were found guilty on Friday of the majority of the 115 charges they faced and, if an appeal fails, they could be hit with unprecedented sanctions, including relegation multiple levels down the pyramid.

Asked on talkSPORT by Pete Graves what he thought City's punishment would be, Winter said: "I think they're going to get hammered.

"I think it will be 50 points [deducted] to trigger a relegation [to the Championship] this season, and then we'll see whether [things are taken further].

"There would obviously have to be some sort of agreement with the EFL if they were going to drop them into League One, but as the great [football finance expert] Kieran Maguire points out, that is possible."

Pressed on whether City could even be expelled from the top four divisions altogether and end up in the National League, Winter said: "That is a huge, huge punishment, but the severity of what they've done, as [former City and FA chairman] David Bernstein eloquently pointed out earlier – and he's a Manchester City fan – they absolutely deserve not just to have the whole book thrown at them but almost the whole library."

On the subject of City's Premier League titles from the 2011/12, 2013/14 and 2017/18 seasons, Winter added: "I would wipe those."

The charges cover the period between 2009 and 2018, with Roberto Mancini, Manuel Pellegrini and Pep Guardiola each winning one of those titles.

Earlier, Bernstein had told talkSPORT City needed to be penalised in a way that 'affected their league status'.

"I would first of all say that financial penalties will not be enough," he began. "We're talking about a club with limitless pockets – money doesn't mean very much as we saw in the last transfer window – and whether it's [a fine of] £100m, £200m, that would not be sufficient.

"Unfortunately – I say all of these things with great sorrow, I really do, as a fan – I think there has to be something that will affect their league status.

2 Bernstein was City chairman from 1998 to 2003, overseeing the club's rise back to the top flight Credit: Getty

"And if it was to be a points deduction, it depends on timing. Because if it was today, with the season just a few games in, and the points deduction had to be something that was terminal as far as their Premier League status was concerned, I worked out you'd have to have something like 80 points deducted, which would mean the club could not recover this season and would go down.

"But if this happens at the end of the season, because of the appeals and so on, it's a different kettle of fish, and then you may be talking about an automatic relegation – to which division I don't know.

"I think it does depend partly on the timing."

City continue to protest their innocence over the charges.

Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak reiterated that point in a letter to fans on Saturday, writing: "Following Friday’s media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began."

Meanwhile, talkSPORT understands that City players do not have relegation release clauses in their contracts.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel explains Trent Alexander-Arnold omission for Spain clash as England wait goes on
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel explains Trent Alexander-Arnold omission for Spain clash as England wait goes on

Trent Alexander-Arnold is still waiting to return to the pitch for England.

The Real Madrid right-back was recalled to the squad for the Three Lions' four Nations League games during this international break, but he had to make do with a place on the bench for Saturday's frustrating 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley.

2 Alexander-Arnold hasn't played for England for almost 16 months Credit: Getty

Trent's long wait to add to England caps

Thomas Tuchel opted to start Alexander-Arnold's former Liverpool teammate Jarell Quansah on the right of his back four, and Quansah played the entire game as Alexander-Arnold watched on.

Left out of England's World Cup squad this summer, Alexander-Arnold hasn't featured for his country since a World Cup qualifier against Andorra in June last year.

The 27-year-old is at least in contention to add to his 34 caps to date in England's upcoming matches, though.

The Three Lions continue their Nations League campaign away to Czechia on Tuesday before a trip to Croatia on Saturday.

They then entertain Czechia the following Tuesday as the extra-long international break wraps up.

There ought to be opportunities for Alexander-Arnold given the inevitable need to rotate, but it does seem Quansah is Tuchel's preferred choice at right-back for the time being.

Tuchel praises 'top class' Quansah

Explaining his defensive tactics after the loss to Spain, the England boss said: "We needed Jarell Quansah’s speed and ability to think as a central defender.

"He was top class at the World Cup; he was top class in training this week; he was excellent in this game."

Speaking after bringing Alexander-Arnold back into the fold, Tuchel insisted 'the door is always open' for players to be recalled.

"They had a good start to the season," Tuchel said of Alexander-Arnold and fellow returning star Cole Palmer – who subsequently withdrew from the squad.

2 Tuchel has kept faith with Quansah at right-back after the Bayer Leverkusen player impressed there at the World Cup Credit: Getty

"They never did something wrong. We just chose different players.

"So now it is a new competition. Some players, some positions, have more injuries. Some have less injuries. Cole has his starts that he always had but he has his numbers back – he has his assists back, he has decisive goals back – so that is why he is in the squad.

"I think he has a point to prove, and the same goes for Trent. He was never off the list. He was never non-selectable for us, and it is his chance to show, come to camp and be the best version of himself."

However, Tuchel later called out Palmer for, in his eyes, 'missing too many opportunities' to represent England.

The Chelsea forward also missed the World Cup after a disappointing 2025/26 campaign but has been in superb form early this season.

Manchester United and Republic of Ireland legend Roy Keane also criticised Palmer.

"I like Palmer; he’s a talented boy," he told ITV, "but he’s got far too many bad habits, for me."

Sports.title: Man United handed huge injury scare as star ruled out of international match with ‘complicated problem’
Sports.content:
Man United handed huge injury scare as star ruled out of international match with ‘complicated problem’

Bruno Fernandes has been ruled out of Portugal's match with Norway.

The Manchester United captain started Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales on Thursday night, but was brought off late in the game.

4 Fernandes will sit out Portugal's second of four Nations League games during the international break Credit: Getty



The injury scare has caused him to sit out of training on Saturday.

Portugal manager Jorge Jesus says he will not risk him for the Nations League clash with Norway on Sunday.

“In the game against Wales, we went in with all the available players but Bruno Fernandes came off with a complicated problem,” Jesus said during his press conference.

“We’ll see what happens until tomorrow. Experience tells me that on the third day not all players manage to recover but that’s the same for Norway as for us.

“However, the player who comes in gives as many guarantees as the one who might come off, that’s what I’ll base my decision on.



“The medical team identified these two players as the most concerning, Nuno Mendes could be available for the game.

“The other case [Fernandes] involves treatment and recovery time. He’s coming off an injury at United, and he told me he’s been playing with that pain for the last three games, which is hindering him.



“It was one of the factors that prevented Bruno from playing at his best against Wales.”

Jesus did stress that it was a precautionary measure and it is hoped he can return for next week's game with Denmark.



He added: “I’ve already spoken to him and I prefer not to risk it in this game so he’s fully fit for the Denmark match.”

4 Fernandes has three Premier League goals this season - all in the same game Credit: Getty

Following the Norway match on Sunday, Portugal will face Denmark on October 1 and then Norway again on October 4.

Bruno Fernandes at Man United

Fernandes' three Premier League goals this season all came in the same game when Man United thrashed Ipswich in August.



The United skipper grabbed a hat-trick, and an assist, in the 5-2 victory.

That has proved to be the Red Devils' only league win for Michael Carrick this season.

They have suffered defeats to Hull and Man City, while drawing with Everton and Fulham.

Fernandes did also get on the scoresheet in their 4-0 Champions League victory over Sabah.



4 Fernandes has been United's standout star in recent years Credit: Getty

Bruno Fernandes' future

Fernandes, whose contract is set to expire next summer, has long been linked with a move away from the club with credible interest from Turkey and Saudi Arabia.

talkSPORT's Adrian Durham, however, argued that the Red Devils should have cashed in on him long ago.

He said on talkSPORT's Fiery Fridays: “I know you love Bruno Fernandes and I get it, those numbers were insane in that lazy season he had last season,”



“He can be an absolute bully, usually against poor sides. I get your love for him but just hear me out on this.

“I think Manchester United made a massive error not selling him in the summer [transfer] window.

“You’re probably fuming inside but hold it in for now.

“Bruno Fernandes has just turned 32, so this summer just gone, Bruno’s stock was the highest it could possibly be. Financially, his worth is reducing and reducing.

“His value, according to AI right now, is £35million. His value in the summer – £87m.



4 United will hope Fernandes does not return with more injury problems Credit: Getty

“On what level of business sense does it make sense to keep a player of that age. He’s never going to do those numbers again.

‘So, United should have sold Bruno in the summer. The Player of the Year award would have inflated the fee even more. United could have got a lot of money for him.

“Here’s the thing, we all know they overspent in midfield and underspent in defence.



“They could’ve addressed that situation and I know United fans are thinking we can’t do anything without Bruno, panic without Bruno. We all know this isn’t true.”

He added: “I think this would have made perfect sense, a player right at his peak. He’s only going to fall to age 32 onwards.

“Those numbers aren’t going to come back, this would have made perfect sense. Manchester United have missed a trick, should have sold Bruno in the summer.

Sports.title: Major concern raised about 2/10 England star who is not at same level since Premier League switch
Sports.content:
Major concern raised about 2/10 England star who is not at same level since Premier League switch

Marc Guehi has not been the same player since joining Manchester City.

That's the assessment of talkSPORT's Tony Cascarino on the England centre-back, who was at fault for the opening goal in Saturday's 3-2 Nations League loss to Spain.

2 Guehi was dispossessed by Lamine Yamal with costly consequences Credit: Getty

'England look really short defensively'

Guehi left Crystal Palace for Man City in January and started well under Pep Guardiola but, now with Enzo Maresca in charge, isn't performing 'anywhere near' his previous levels, feels Cascarino.

Speaking on the Weekend Sports Breakfast after England's defeat at Wembley, the former Chelsea and Republic of Ireland striker said: "Defensively, England look really short at the moment. No one stood out in the back line last night.

"I don't think Marc Guehi is playing anywhere near as well as he was a year ago with the performances he put in for Crystal Palace that got him the move to Manchester City.

"Marc Guehi was playing superbly this time last year.

"After initially a good start at City, I don't think he's played to the same level as what he did at Palace.

"If you're looking at small margins, one of the reasons Thomas Tuchel got the job was because they felt like they needed a manager or coach to get them over the line. They've got a team that needs to get over the line."

England on the wrong end of Wembley thriller

England were back in action for the first time since finishing third at this summer's World Cup, where Tuchel drew intense criticism for his tactical approach as the Three Lions blew a 1-0 lead to lose 2-1 to Argentina in the semi-finals.

And Guehi endured a nightmare start to the game against newly crowned world champions Spain.

He was caught in possession on the edge of his own box, allowing Lamine Yamal to pounce and give the visitors the lead inside two minutes.

England came roaring back through goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane to lead at half-time – but after Kane slipped and hit the underside of the crossbar with a penalty, Spain responded courtesy of substitutes Alex Baena, who capitalised on a stray pass from Guehi's City teammate Nico O'Reilly, and Mikel Oyarzabal.

2 Mikel Oyarzabal scored Spain's winning goal against England, just as he did in the Euro 2024 final Credit: Getty

Low marks for Guehi and O'Reilly

And Guehi's difficult night saw him among the three England players who received 2/10 ratings from talkSPORT's Adrian Durham.

Durham asked England legend Stuart Pearce on air whether Guehi and O'Reilly might have been distracted after City were found guilty on Friday of breaching Premier League financial rules.

But Pearce wasn't sure that news played any part in the pair's sub-par displays.

"I wouldn't think so," he replied. "I'll be very, very surprised if that is the case.

"The bottom line is City are so used to dominating the ball, sometimes they've got to check out – recycle it and whatever.

"Tonight there was some good pressing from the Spaniards, and it caught us out."

Sports.title: Erling Haaland transfer release clause update emerges amid Man City relegation threat
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland and his Manchester City teammates do not have relegation release clauses in their contracts, talkSPORT understands.

On Friday, Man City were found guilty of the overwhelming majority of the 115 charges they faced relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.



3 Haaland is right at the top of the list of players City would face a battle to keep hold of if they were to be relegated Credit: Getty

Haaland in the Championship?

And the potential sanctions against the club, which have yet to be determined, include a points deduction so hefty it would effectively relegate them from the top flight – or worse.

talkSPORT also understands the EFL, who administer the second to fourth tiers of English football, are prepared to try and keep City out of their competitions if necessary.

And one of the numerous big questions right now is where would relegation leave City's star players?



With no relegation clauses, the club wouldn't have to let players go on the cheap, but it's almost inconceivable that the likes of Haaland, Ruben Dias and Gianluigi Donnarumma would be content with anything less than Premier League and Champions League football.

As such, were City to find themselves dropping down to the Championship or lower, one would expect a whole raft of big-name departures.



talkSPORT previously reported that Barcelona were keen on signing Haaland.

The three-time Premier League Golden Boot-winning striker still has eight years left on his contract at the Etihad Stadium, having agreed a lengthy extension last year.



Indeed, according to Transfermarkt, only two senior City players are set to become free agents at the end of this season: Mateo Kovacic and Marcus Bettinelli.

However, it could be some time yet before City are faced with the nightmarish situation of having to sell their stars.

It's anticipated that the club will appeal against whatever punishment may come their way, meaning the saga could rumble on for months if not years yet.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak continues to maintain the club's innocence.



3 Khaldoon Al Mubarak (left) says City will not let people 'undermine their momentum' Credit: Getty

'So much noise' around City

In a letter to fans on Saturday, he wrote: "Following Friday’s media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

"I ask you to please carefully read the statement below, which we gave on Friday, and the statement we issued in February 2023 (also below). Every word matters and holds true.



"While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our Club. We will not give them that opportunity."

Top of the Premier League as it paused for the international break, City return to action with a trip to Liverpool on October 11.

Sports.title: Referee calls players back onto pitch after blowing for half-time early in EFL chaos
Sports.content:
Referee calls players back onto pitch after blowing for half-time early in EFL chaos

Oldham Athletic players were fuming with referee Isaac Searle when he blew his half-time whistle too early against Salford City.

Salford were 2-1 up in their 4-1 League Two victory at Boundary Park when four minutes of time were added onto the end of the first half.



3 There were almost two minutes still to play when Searle blew for the break Credit: Sky Sports Football YouTube

A little over two of those minutes were played when Searle blew for the interval, sparking bemusement from fans inside the ground.

Oldham star Keenan Appiah-Forson quickly realised the mistake and walked to the official whilst holding up four fingers.

Meanwhile, his teammate Jamie Robson was visibly livid with Searle, who had repeatedly shouted 'Relax!'



Mike Fondop also joined in with the protests as the referee assessed what had happened.

Searle then realised that he did in fact blow his whistle too early, and called the players back onto the pitch for the remaining minutes.



Club staff were already on the pitch and preparing for the half-time entertainment, but had to temporarily return to the side.

Has a referee blown too early before?

The bizarre scenes drew parallels with Tunisia v Mali the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations.



Referee Janny Sikazwe called time on the match before 90 minutes were played on two occasions.

As they chased a late equaliser in what was ultimately a 1-0 defeat, Tunisia players and staff furiously protested the decision.

They then refused to play on when Mali returned around 40 minutes later for the remaining moments, and so the match finally ended.

3 Oldham defender Robson was angry at the official, whilst Appiah-Forson made it clear how long was left to play Credit: Sky Sports Football YouTube



3 Searle was quick to realise his timing error and brought the players back on for the rest of stoppage time Credit: Sky Sports Football YouTube

Speaking after the match, Salford boss Peter Cklamovski addressed the wild scenes in Oldham.

"There was a little bit of chaos in the last 10 minutes of the first half when the referee lost his way, but half-time came at a good time to regroup," he said.

"And the response from the players was good and set the game up for us to win in the second half."



Oldham sit 20th in the table whilst Salford, co-owned by Manchester United legends David Beckham and Gary Neville, are seventh.

Salford lost all of their opening three league fixtures, but have now won three of their last four in an unbeaten run.

They are in contention for promotion to League One this season.

Sports.title: Former Man City chairman David Bernstein expects club to LOSE Premier League status after being found guilty of vast majority of 115 charges: 'Money won't be enough'
Sports.content:
Former Man City chairman David Bernstein expects club to LOSE Premier League status after being found guilty of vast majority of 115 charges: 'Money won't be enough'

Manchester City's former chairman David Bernstein believes punishment handed to the club after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules must affect their top flight status.

Daily Mail Sport reported that the Premier League has succeeded in proving all of the substantive claims against Man City, with the club found guilty of the 'vast majority' of the 115 charges of financial rule breaking.

An appeal from Man City is considered an inevitability, with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak declaring on Saturday that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’.

Bernstein, who was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as Football Association chair 2011-13, has warned that financial penalties will not be enough of a punishment.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Bernstein stressed the fines would not be sufficient as he cited their vast spending in the previous transfer window.

Man City spent £440million in the summer and equalled the British transfer record signing £125million Enzo Fernandez.

Man City's former chairman David Bernstein believes the club's Premier League status is at risk after they were found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 rule break charges

Bernstein was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as FA chair 2011-13

Bernstein believes that while the club's wealth would render a fine insufficient, Man City could face automatic relegation or a points deduction that effectively ensures they will drop out of the top flight.

'I would first of all say that financial penalties will not be enough,' Bernstein said.

'We're talking about a club with limitless pockets – money doesn't mean very much as we saw in the last transfer window – and whether it's [a fine of] £100m, £200m, that would not be sufficient.

'Unfortunately – I say all of these things with great sorrow, I really do, as a fan – I think there has to be something that will affect their league status.

'And if it was to be a points deduction, it depends on timing.

'Because if it was today, with the season just a few games in, and the points deduction had to be something that was terminal as far as their Premier League status was concerned, I worked out you'd have to have something like 80 points deducted, which would mean the club could not recover this season and would go down.

'But if this happens at the end of the season, because of the appeals and so on, it's a different kettle of fish, and then you may be talking about an automatic relegation – to which division I don't know.

'I think it does depend partly on the timing.'

Bernstien suggested Man City's wealth would make a financial penalty for the club 'insufficient'

Man City enjoyed staggering success during the years covered by the Premier League charges

Man City, who have always strongly denied wrongdoing, were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League with a hearing concluding in December 2024.

Their statement that February insisted that they were 'surprised' by the charges.

The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period.

The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

They were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023.

Between the years mentioned, Manchester City won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League, four FA Cups and seven EFL Cups.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday that the verdict will trigger a series of legal claims for as much as £800million.

In late 2024, Arsenal, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester United served formal notices reserving their right to take action in the event that City – who could now face expulsion from the top flight – be found guilty.

Representatives have already begun putting together a case on how much they feel they have a claim for, pointing out that they have lost potential income on the back of City’s cheating.

On Saturday, the club hit back in the shape of a strong statement from chairman Al Mubarak, who declared that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’.

Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak insisted the club remains confident of clearing their name and ‘proving innocence’

In a lengthy statement, Al Mubarak seemed to make the suggestion that the process had not been fair. He asked fans to study a statement made on Friday by the club closely. That statement read: ‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'

In his message to fans, he wrote: ‘The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.

‘There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

‘While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity.’

Sports.title: Man United hit with injury scares as captain Bruno Fernandes is ruled out of Portugal clash with 'complicated problem'... and Patrick Dorgu is taken off early playing for Denmark
Sports.content:
Man United hit with injury scares as captain Bruno Fernandes is ruled out of Portugal clash with 'complicated problem'... and Patrick Dorgu is taken off early playing for Denmark

Manchester United are braced for a double injury blow with captain Bruno Fernandes ruled out of Portugal's Nations League clash with Norway on Sunday and Denmark's Patrick Dorgu forced off early against Wales.

Fernandes, 32, was substituted late on in in Thursday's 1-0 win over Wales in Lisbon and manager Jorge Jesus has confirmed he will play no part in Oslo - as well as claiming he has played through pain in recent games for United.

'In the game against Wales, we went in with all the available players but Bruno Fernandes came off with a complicated problem,' said Jesus.

Jesus added: 'He said he’s been dealing with that pain for about three games, and that was one of the factors that prevented him from being at his usual level against Wales.

'He was my player, I know him perfectly. I’ve already spoken to him. I prefer not to risk him in this game and have him clean and in good physical condition for the Denmark game (in Copenhagen on Thursday).'

His absence means the midfielder will be denied a second clash with Erling Haaland this month, having suffered a 1-0 defeat in the Manchester derby at Old Trafford which saw the Norway striker score the only goal.

Bruno Fernandes featured in the 1-0 win against Wales but was forced off late on

Dorgu, meanwhile, was substituted after going down just 30 minutes into Denmark's clash with Wales in Copenhagen.

Any serious injury would add to United's worries, with Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo both withdrawing from England’s squad and forward Benjamin Sesko recovering from a shin issue that has seen him miss Slovenia's internationals this month.

But the club will be most concerned about Fernandes, who has played 90 minutes in all five of United Premier League matches so far this season as well as the entirety of their 4-0 Champions League win over Sabah.

He was also brought off the bench in an attempt to rescue his side after they blew a two-goal lead at home to Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

United return to action on Saturday October 10, at home to Tottenham. They have endured a frustrated start to the season under Michael Carrick with their sole Premier League win coming against Ipswich - in which they needed a Fernandes hat-trick to secure a 5-2 victory.

Sports.title: Tom Banton's blistering 126 ends difficult English summer on a high with crushing win over Sri Lanka... as happy captain Harry Brook revels in 'near-perfect' display
Sports.content:
Tom Banton's blistering 126 ends difficult English summer on a high with crushing win over Sri Lanka... as happy captain Harry Brook revels in 'near-perfect' display

England’s long – and at times difficult – summer ended on a high as a maiden international century for Tom Banton set up a crushing 223-run win over Sri Lanka.

There were runs too for Jordan Cox, who hit a sparkling 76 off 52 balls as Jos Buttler’s injury replacement, plus a contender for the ball of the season from Sonny Baker, who found Pathum Nissanka’s outside edge in the second over of the chase with an unplayable delivery that swung and took off as if from a trampoline.

Above all, England were able to breathe more freely after blowing their run-chase at Headingley on Thursday, a meltdown which raised the possibility that the white-ball progress made under Harry Brook might be undermined at the last.

Instead, Brook – who contributed a typically effervescent 77 – could celebrate a third successive ODI series win, England’s first such sequence since 2023, when their opponents included Bangladesh and Ireland. Since replacing Buttler as captain last year, he has presided over 33 white-ball victories and only 11 defeats, with England’s T20 form especially hot.

But the next World Cup, starting in southern Africa in just over a year’s time, is a 50-over affair, and Brook must be quietly thrilled not only that the talk is once more about the actual cricket rather than off-field misadventure, but that options are starting to emerge after some fallow years for the one-day team.

Banton is chief among them, having taken his chance to stand in for the injured Jacob Bethell with aplomb. After making 73 three days earlier, he looked in no mood to miss out on three figures, using his height and power to launch five sixes in a blistering 105-ball 126 that will ensure Bethell’s return is no gimme.

"Beauty from Sonny Baker!"



What a start for England 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wLQ9R6J2pv — Sky Sports Cricket (@SkyCricket) September 27, 2026

Tom Banton hit a series of superb boundaries in his innings of 126 as England posted 355-7

Banton was able to celebrate his first century in style as he helped England to a series win

His first six, an uppercut off Dilshan Madushanka, showed off his hand-eye coordination. Later, he pulled Madushanka for six more, then deposited his next ball over long-off with exquisite timing.

‘To get over the line is a feeling I can’t explain,’ said Banton. ‘There are times when you’re sat there in your room wondering if that chance with England will ever come again. It’s been an amazing day.’

All the while, Brook was moving through the gears after a sticky start against the left-arm spin of Dunith Wellalage. After labouring to 10 off 24 balls, including a bad drop at wide slip by Nissanka on seven, he smashed 67 off his next 42, before slapping seamer Asitha Fernando to mid-off.

It meant Brook finished the international summer with 10 scores of at least 50 from 23 innings, but only one century. And yet his cross-format average is 50, and his strike-rate 114 – remarkable when you consider 11 of those innings have been in Tests. Ominously for opponents, it feels as if there is room for improvement.

The icing on England’s cake was provided by Cox. As Bethell’s stand-in at No 3 in the Test side, he took three half-centuries off Pakistan. Here, he made light of Buttler’s absence as 104 came from the last 10 overs. Until now, Cox’s ODI career had consisted of three underwhelming appearances in the Caribbean in late 2024. He had not made a one-day fifty of any kind. On this evidence, he looks hard to ignore.

‘I thought that was near perfect,’ said Brook. ‘Everyone chipped in beautifully. We’re building towards a squad where, if someone does go down, someone else can come in and perform. Coxy was exceptional, and I was really proud of the way Bants played.’

It was a less fruitful day for two more experienced players. Ben Duckett was bowled for a duck by a beauty from Madushanka, while Joe Root made just 18 before he fell lbw to Janith Liyanage. Of his 13 dismissals in the three international formats this season, nine have been leg-before.

Harry Brook capped off an eventful cricketing summer on a high with a 2-1 series victory

For only the second time in his career, he has gone through a home summer without a hundred for either England or Yorkshire. Since the only other instance came in 2020, when Covid limited him to 11 knocks for England and none at all for his county, 2026 is very much the outlier.

Sri Lanka had never knocked off more than 322, so a target of 357 looked beyond them even before the irrepressible Baker undid Nissanka and celebrated his first ODI wicket with a characteristic leap and punch of the air.

Gus Atkinson bounced out both Mendises – Kamindu and Kushal – and Jofra Archer’s direct hit did for Pavan Rathnayake. Cox had dislodged the bails with his gloves before the ball arrived, but the fact that Archer’s deadeye throw uprooted the stump meant Cox’s blunder went unpunished.

The rest was a procession, with Liam Dawson – preferred to Rehan Ahmed – hoovering up three wickets, and Sri Lanka were all out for 132 with more than 20 overs of their innings unused. An anti-climax, perhaps, but England weren’t complaining.

Sports.title: Man City could still lift the Premier League title THIS season despite being found guilty of 'vast majority' of rule breaches - with hefty legal delays expected over appeal process
Sports.content:
Man City could still lift the Premier League title THIS season despite being found guilty of 'vast majority' of rule breaches - with hefty legal delays expected over appeal process

Legal experts expect Manchester City to be free to lift this season’s Premier League trophy, despite having been found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them.

City’s anticipated appeal, hinted at by chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak in a statement at the weekend, could ultimately see them take the case to the High Court.

Experts say that the grounds for a successful appeal, which would have to be heard by a separate and newly convened independent commission, are narrow. But if an appeal failed, City could seek a judicial review of the commission's findings at the High Court.

To do so, they would need to demonstrate that the Premier League acted outside its powers or reached a conclusion which no reasonable authority could have reached. If either could be proved by City's legal team, the outcome could be quashed. But City would need the High Court’s permission to make a judicial review application and the bar is high.

Legal experts expect Manchester City to be free to lift this season’s Premier League trophy

Man City were found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges brought against them on Friday

It is unclear how much of the independent commission's findings will be made public. Most arbitration processes have strict confidentiality rules in place. Though City and the Premier League are likely to have waived some of the right to confidentiality, it is possible that only a summary or redacted version of the judgement will be published.

The likely legal delays mean it is entirely possible that Premier League executives may be left to watch City lift the title at the Etihad Stadium next spring, should they maintain their strong start to the season. The side are currently three points clear at the top of the table. ‘The final outcome of this case, particularly in relation to sanctions, may still take considerable time to be resolved,’ said Chris Partington, a lawyer at Brandsmiths.

The independent commission’s findings are likely to be straining relations between the UK and the United Arab Emirates, whose sovereign wealth funds have been embedded in Manchester's urban development during Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s time as the Mayor of Greater Manchester.

Asked if City should be stripped of previous titles, Burnham said on Friday: ‘People shouldn’t jump to those kind of conclusions. I think we would all need to study the independent commission’s report in some detail.’

Sports.title: Jason Cundy reveals how he became football's most notorious wind-up merchant, the truth behind THAT Ange Postecoglou mask - and insists he will never let up on Spurs foe Jamie O'Hara
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy reveals how he became football's most notorious wind-up merchant, the truth behind THAT Ange Postecoglou mask - and insists he will never let up on Spurs foe Jamie O'Hara

Jason Cundy's public life seems to have one main purpose: to make Jamie O'Hara as miserable and mortified as possible.

Cundy is, by now, football's biggest wind-up merchant. It is a role he revels in, and one which has brought talkSPORT's Sports Bar show immense popularity on social media.

He is in his element with that ridiculous Ange Postecoglou mask stretched comically over his head, firing wisecracks and shameful stats about Tottenham over at O'Hara, who can only sit with his head in his hands and take the mockery.

So, how much pleasure does Cundy take in tearing his radio co-pilot to shreds?

'A huge amount,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I don't feel for Jamie.

'Every single game, they lose or manage not to score. Never has the expression 'the gift that keeps giving' been more appropriate to Spurs at any other time.'

Jason Cundy has become football's biggest wind-up merchant due to Tottenham's decline

His Ange Postecoglou mask and jibes have been a menace to talkSPORT co-host Jamie O'Hara's

Cundy even turned up to O'Hara's wedding wearing the mask and takes 'huge' pleasure in annoying him

There is something relentlessly funny about the Postecoglou mask. Something about the sheer smugness of it, the expressionlessness, as O'Hara sits a metre away having meltdown after meltdown as this warped face just... watches him, unblinking.

O'Hara couldn't even escape the haunting face at his wedding to Keziah Grubb this year. On one of the biggest days of O'Hara's life, there was Cundy, head wrapped tight in his favourite Postecoglou-themed plaything.

In the week after our interview, Cundy posts no fewer than eight clips of him ripping into O'Hara's former club Tottenham, who are bottom of the Premier League and winless. In one, he diagnoses the club with 'Spursitis', something nobody in football wants.

TalkSPORT has often fallen foul of accusations of ragebaiting its listeners too much, but the mask is almost universally loved by its viewers on social media – unless they're Tottenham fans.

'I came up with the idea to get masked because talkSPORT is so visual,' Cundy says. 'I didn't realise it would take on a whole life of its own.

'We bought them from South America and we order a new mask every year.

'We bought the Ange mask when he was the manager at Nottingham Forest, and by the time the mask turned up he'd got sacked, so I had to find a role for it.

'We've got a Gary Neville one, an Arne Slot one, and now we've got a Jamie Carragher one, that'll come out soon.

Cundy was speaking to Daily Mail Sport on behalf of TENA Men, who were sponsoring the 2026 Prostate United launch event

'It's the same mask each time. It absolutely stinks! It's got a weird smell about it. I tell Jamie it's the smell of failure. That's what it stinks of.

'I did clean it but think it's best to just leave it now, just to do what it does, somehow just let it lie in its own stink, and the worse the mask gets the worse Spurs get.'

Cundy was speaking to Daily Mail Sport on behalf of TENA Men, who were sponsoring the 2026 Prostate United launch event. The 56-year-old is a survivor of testicular cancer, so the issue of men's health is close to his heart.

'I have a voice to speak and spread a message - go and get yourself checked for testicular cancer, or get a PSA check. You have a duty to yourself and your family.'

He has brought his cancer experience onto the airwaves before, recording a long-form interview with talkSPORT on the subject in 2022, showing a deeper, more sensitive side to his personality than the joker we typically get to hear.

There is a pitfall in the show's reliance on Spurs being bad: namely, what if the north Londoners start being good?

Maybe O'Hara would then have the chance to turn the tables on his mate and have a dig at his alma mater Chelsea.

In any case, Cundy isn't too worried about Tottenham becoming sensations overnight.

Tottenham are bottom of the table and winless this season under manager Roberto De Zerbi

'You can't finish 17th, 17th, and go into a new season expecting there to be a huge dramatic change,' he says.

'Spurs aren't in the big six. Spurs would be in the big six in the Championship if they're not too careful.

'If they carry on being c***, Roberto De Zerbi will get the sack. That's football. That goes for every manager, not just him. But because it's Spurs, history is repeating itself.

'They've signed players that don't score goals: Omar Marmoush scored eight last season, Savio four. Mathys Tel, meh, four. Richarlison's not in the Premier League squad.

'If you put Erling Haaland up top, he still wouldn't score. They don't create chances.'

Jason Cundy was speaking on behalf of TENA Men, who sponsored the 2026 Prostate United launch event. To find out more about Prostate Cancer UK’s football fundraising challenge visit – prostateunited.prostatecanceruk.org/

Sports.title: Liverpool suffer double injury blow as Alexander Isak withdraws from Sweden duty with thigh problem... before Cody Gakpo is forced off playing for Netherlands
Sports.content:
Liverpool suffer double injury blow as Alexander Isak withdraws from Sweden duty with thigh problem... before Cody Gakpo is forced off playing for Netherlands

Liverpool have a double injury headache with star Alexander Isak cutting short his international duty with Sweden and Cody Gakpo being forced off just 17 minutes into Netherlands' clash with Serbia.

Isak, who has enjoyed his best-ever start to a Premier League season, will be assessed by Liverpool's medical staff at the AXA Training Centre.

The forward scored in Sweden's 2-1 win over Romania on Friday but Sweden boss Graham Potter later said: 'Isak has a minor thigh problem.

'It's nothing serious, but due to the number of matches in a short period of time, he won't be able to take part.

'It's frustrating for both him and us, but it is what it is.'

He was also spotted with a blood-soaked sock after a heavy challenge.

Alexander Isak has withdrawn from Sweden duty with a 'minor injury' after a 'heavy stamp'

He has enjoyed a fine start to the Premier League campaign, scoring four goals in five games

'You can see it... It was a heavy stamp,' he told reporters in the mixed zone.

'Those of you who have played might know that it takes a few minutes for the pain to subside, but it was okay.’

Winger Gakpo, meanwhile, went down holding his left ankle 17 minutes into Netherlands' Nations League clash in Serbia on Sunday afternoon. He appeared to be visibly in pain and Liverpool fans will have their fingers crossed that the injuries to both stars are minor.

Isak missed 30 matches for club and country due to various injuries. The £125million record signing suffered a broken leg and was sidelined for months after a robust challenge by Tottenham's Micky van de Ven in December.

It left him unavailable until April and unable to gain any momentum in a debut season where he scored just four times in all competitions after signing from Newcastle.

He has started this season much more like himself, banging in four goals in five Premier League games, a personal best start to the campaign.

The 27-year-old scored in the 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest, struck both goals in the 2-0 win over Ipswich, and netted the 1-0 winner against Bournemouth.

Cody Gakpo went down in pain early on in Netherlands' clash with Serbia on Sunday

Sweden's statement on his exit described the injury as 'minor', but it means he will play no part in their upcoming Nations League games against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Romania.

Gakpo, meanwhile, has scored twice for Liverpool in the Premier League this season. A proposed move to Manchester City fell through before deadline day but the 27-year-old appears to have responded well.

Alongside scoring goals, Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola wants Isak to step up by leading Liverpool's press with more ferocity.

Daily Mail Sport has reported how Iraola has even been showing Isak clips of academy graduate Lewis Koumas as a model of off-the-ball work.

Isak seems to be getting the message, telling BBC Sport recently that defending is an 'attacking weapon'.

Sports.title: 'We feel cheated... we want our FA Cup': Tony Pulis calls for Stoke City to be awarded trophy 15 years after losing final to Man City at Wembley as storm over 115 charges verdict rages on
Sports.content:
Former Stoke City boss Tony Pulis has said he feels 'cheated' having lost the 2011 FA Cup final to Manchester City, after the club were found guilty of the ‘vast majority’ of the Premier League's 115 charges against them for financial rule breaking. Daily Mail Sport reported that the Premier League has succeeded in proving all of the substantive claims against Man City. An appeal from Man City is considered an inevitability, with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak declaring on Saturday that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’. Former Man United stars David de Gea and Rio Ferdinand have already called on Man City to be stripped of their 2011-12 Premier League title following the verdict. Fans of rival clubs have also called for the club to be stripped of trophies won during the period covered by the charges. Man City's glittering era of success under their Abu Dhabi ownership was launched when they beat Stoke City 1-0 in the 2011 FA Cup final, representing the club's first major honour since 1976. Tony Pulis admits he feels 'cheated' having lost the 2011 FA Cup final to Manchester City, after the club were found guilty of the ‘vast majority’ of the Premier League's 115 charges Man City overcame Pulis' Stoke City side 1-0 at Wembley to win their first major trophy since 1976 Yaya Toure scored the only goal of the FA Cup final to win the trophy for Roberto Mancini's side Yaya Toure scored the only goal of the final in the 74th minute at Wembley. Pulis, who led underdogs Stoke into the final, told the BBC that fans of the club have contacted him to ask whether they will be awarded the FA Cup. The Welshman, whose second spell as Stoke boss lasted from 2006 to 2013, admitted he now feels 'cheated' after being beaten by Man City, following Friday's verdict. 'We lost, but to a team that have been found guilty of breaking the financial rules set out by the Premier League,' Pulis told the BBC. 'In doing so, they did not just beat Stoke in an FA Cup final, they collected a stack of titles and went on to completely dominate English football for more than a decade. 'So, with those rules having been broken, what will the punishment be? 'Well, I know all Stoke supporters will be demanding that City pass the trophy over and every club that has been affected by their actions will be considering their legal options. 'I don't expect Manchester City to phone me or the club up and offer back the 2011 FA Cup and the winners' medals their players received. 'I don't seriously believe any other trophies and titles will be handed back over either. A points deduction and a massive fine feels far more likely.' Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of their 115 Premier League rule-break charges The club have maintained that they are innocent throughout the process and are expected to appeal HOW THE TEAMS LINED UP Man City: Hart, Richards, Kompany, Lescott, Kolorov, De Jong, Barry, Toure, David Silva, Balotelli, Tevez. Subs: Given, Zabaleta, Boyata, Milner, Johnson, Vieria, Dzeko Manager: Roberto Mancini Stoke: Sorensen, Wilkinson, Shawcross, Huth, Wilson, Pennant, Whelan, Delap, Etherington, Jones, Walters. Subs: Nash, Collins, Faye, Pugh, Diao, Whitehead, Carew Manager: Tony Pulis Man City, who have always strongly denied wrongdoing, were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League with a hearing concluding in December 2024. Their statement that February insisted that they were 'surprised' by the charges. The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period. The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13. They were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023. Between the years mentioned, Manchester City won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League, four FA Cups and seven EFL Cups. Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday that the verdict will trigger a series of legal claims for as much as £800million. In late 2024, Arsenal, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester United served formal notices reserving their right to take action in the event that City – who could now face expulsion from the top flight – be found guilty. Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak (left) has insisted his club are innocent of the charges they have been found guilty of Representatives have already begun putting together a case on how much they feel they have a claim for, pointing out that they have lost potential income on the back of City’s cheating. On Saturday, the club hit back in the shape of a strong statement from chairman Al Mubarak, who declared that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’. In a lengthy statement, Al Mubarak seemed to make the suggestion that the process had not been fair. He asked fans to study a statement made on Friday by the club closely. That statement read: ‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.' In his message to fans, he wrote: ‘The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began. ‘There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies. ‘While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity.’

Sports.title: Irish snooker legend Ken Doherty responds after being bizarrely dragged into Israeli footballer's 'gun' celebration controversy
Sports.content:
Irish snooker legend Ken Doherty responds after being bizarrely dragged into Israeli footballer's 'gun' celebration controversy

Irish snooker legend Ken Doherty has been unexpectedly dragged into the controversy over an Israeli footballer who was accused of celebrating a goal with a gun gesture.

And the former world champion, 57, has simply responded with a laughing face emoji at the clip of his name being pulled into the scandal.

Israel forward Sayed Abu Farchi was sent off in the second half of his side's defeat against Austria, having taken the corner flag out the ground and appeared to mimic a gunshot.

Fans were left stunned and judged the move to be in bad taste, given Israel are at war with Palestine, with more than 70,000 people killed by Israeli attacks to date.

But Israel's delegation has now insisted that Farchi was imitating a snooker hit.

‘We contend that the first yellow card was incorrect and the second, which led to his sending off, stemmed from a misinterpretation by the match referee and the VAR team,’ said their head of communications Shlomi Barzel.

Irish snooker legend responded with a laughing emoji after being unexpectedly dragged into the controversy over an Israeli football controversy

Israel's Sayed Abu Farchi was sent off on Thursday after appearing to mimic a gunshot

His manager has leapt to his defence amid questions on the Colorado Rapids' midfielder's actions in the game

‘Anybody familiar with Sayed Abu Farchi knows that his celebration after scoring the equaliser was in imitation of a snooker player, such as the legendary Ken Doherty for example.’

Abu Farchi protested with Bulgarian official Georgi Kabakov at the time, insisting he should have stayed on the field.

But he was already on a yellow card, and Kabakov opted to show him a second booking, resulting in his dismissal.

Israel manager Ran Ben-Shimon leapt to the defence of the Colorado Rapids midfielder after the game, insisting the celebration is regularly carried out by Abu Farchi without punishment.

'I've seen it before and everyone can check,' said Ben-Shimon. 'When this young player scores, in the Israeli national team or the MLS or anywhere he plays, he celebrates in the same situation again and again and he never gets a yellow card about it.

'He didn't know about it, this is his way to celebrate every goal he scores. He's a young player, I'm sure this lesson will stay with him a long time, he made a mistake.'

UEFA rules, meanwhile, suggest the referee was right to show a second yellow card.

They say a player must be booked for 'gesturing or acting in a provocative, derisory or inflammatory way'. Removing the corner flag is also yellow card worthy.

Israel have already been a focus of attention this week with the country to face the Republic of Ireland in two matches over the current international break.

The Israeli FA angrily took to social media on Monday to hit back at Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson's comments when he used the word 'genocide' in previewing the upcoming fixtures.

The Icelandic boss used forceful language in defending his team as they prepare to take the field against a side that the Football Association of Ireland wanted to have suspended from competitions.

'And I've said before, we're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide,' he said at the weekend. 'So, we're playing against Israel. We're not playing with Israel.'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson came under fire from the Israel FA for saying his team will be 'playing against genocide' this week

As reports circulated that the Israelis were considering a complaint to UEFA, the Israeli FA posted on X on Monday night: 'We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way,' the post on X stated.

'Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by the Republic of Ireland team coach.

'We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them.'

The matches will take place at neutral venues on Sunday and then again on October 4.

Second-choice Ireland goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu has pulled out of the clash and insisted he isn't against Israelis or Jews – but against the atrocities in Gaza.

After a tense day where the match was plunged into doubt, Bazunu wrote on Instagram: 'Representing my country means everything to me.

'I have the utmost respect for every single one of my teammates, the manager, his staff and the Irish people.

View this post on Instagram

Ireland goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu has withdrawn from the squad for the clash with Israel

'However, I have reached a decision that I have not taken lightly. I am a man of strong faith and try my best to be a person of character and principle, therefore I feel it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel.

'My decision is based purely upon my belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong. It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition to the Israeli people or the Jewish community but against the atrocities in the region.

'There are few times when you get a chance in life to stand for something bigger and I strongly believe that this is one of them.'

A source close to the player told The Mail on Sunday the Dubliner's family is proud of him for standing up for his beliefs.

'Gavin is a hero,' they said. ´What he's done took great courage. His family is proud.'

Sports.title: New-look international break has its merits but more club vs country rows loom
Sports.content:
New-look international break has its merits but more club vs country rows loom

England players have started a run of four games across 10 days during this new extended international break but the idea is all but certain to spark more club v country clashes

View 3 Images The new extended international break is now in full swing

The new-look international break is certain to cause even more club v country rows.

‌



For a start, it is surely unthinkable that an England player will start all four games in the ten day window. After the opening game with Spain at Wembley, England travel to Prague to face the Czech Republic on Tuesday night. That is followed by Croatia in Rijeka next Saturday tea time and then they place the Czech Republic again in the return fixture at Wembley on Tuesday, October 6.

‌



Bearing in mind there were five withdrawals before the squad even got together - Cole Palmer, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Tino Livramento and Declan Rice - Premier League clubs are clearly anxious to protect their players from burnout.

‌



Rice and Palmer were both described as “load management” with the Arsenal midfielder still suffering a hangover from the World Cup on the back of a marathon season when he played 69 games for club and country.

But while Rice’s absence is understandable, you would also expect other clubs to think it was unfair if some players get three weeks off while theirs are expected to play several games across the window.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

You have already seen Arsenal forward Kai Havertz suffer a suspected hamstring issue while away with Germany and Sunderland’s Holland striker Brian Bobbey went off with a similar issue in the same game.

That has already got fans complaining about the new-look international break and the impact it might have on their clubs.

‌



It is a good idea in principle. It means that you get two international windows for the Nations League rather than the previous three which should reduce some of the disruption to the Premier League fixture list. This one is the long one whereas the international break in November is short, two games and you only lose one weekend because the Premier League starts again straight afterwards.

The players get proper time with their nations, they get a good get-together and the Nations League does throw up some heavyweight fixtures.

By the end of the International window, England will have played Spain, Croatia and the Czech Republic twice. The opening round of Nations League fixtures pitted Holland against Germany and there are decent fixtures.

‌



View 3 Images England have an extended period to work with Thomas Tuchel (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

England captain Harry Kane talked about wanting to play in all four games and Thomas Tuchel has only ended up with 23 players so if you do the sums then it is unlikely you will get a complete 11 changes from game to game.

It means some players will get a lot of football and others not so much. That has always been the case but this window seems to have compounded it.

‌



What is surprising is that more Premier League managers have not publicly criticised this new-look international window. On the back of a World Cup, it feels wrong that players are being asked to play four intense games in the space of ten days. You are certain to get injuries, withdrawals and issues. England really need this campaign to work because dropping out of the top tier in the Nations League affects seeding, qualifying and also the standard of games which stretches teams.

The Nations League is a brilliant invention. The best thing to happen to international football in a long time because you get competitive games rather than meaningless friendlies. It’s also another chance to win an international trophy.

View 3 Images Arsenal's Kai Havertz has already sustained an injury during the break (Image: Lars Baron/Getty Images)

‌



There is no easy slot for the fixtures and whether this new-look window is a success will probably be judged on who gets injured. That is just football.

But England face two tricky away games, the second of why is played largely behind closed doors which is so unfair on England fans.

Croatia were banned from having fans in Rijeka by UEFA and yet there will be several thousand school kids (accompanied by some adults) and also around 100 lucky England fans with a very limited number of tickets recently on sale.

Article continues below

International football matters but pitching it in the right way in the calendar feels so important.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland's dad admitted his son could leave Man City and named six clubs he could join
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's dad admitted his son could leave Man City and named six clubs he could join

Erling Haaland signed a nine-and-a-half-year contract with Manchester City, but his dad believes he could be on the move soon

View 2 Images Erling Haaland's dad believes his son could leave Manchester City (Image: Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images)

Alf-Inge Haaland once claimed his son won't be at Manchester City forever - and could even leave at the end of this season. The ex-Premier League star named several clubs his son could join in the future, including Barcelona, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



Haaland Sr's words have resurfaced after City were found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges they faced for financial rule breaches. The club could face points deductions, be stripped of trophies and even be relegated to the lower leagues.

‌



Haaland was slated to speak ahead of Norway's clash with Portugal, but was removed from media duties. TV2 reported that the striker has been replaced by Benfica duo Andreas Schjelderup and Fredrik Aursnes.

‌



Long before the news broke about City's charges, Haaland Sr addressed his son's potential career and admitted he expects him to compete in all the top leagues around the world. In 2022, the ex-Leeds man appeared on the documentary, Haaland: The Big Decision, and was frank about what he believes will happen.

Premier League bosses urged to immediately RELEGATE Man City after 115 charges verdict READ MORE :

The 53-year-old said: "I think Erling wants to prove his abilities in all leagues. Then he can stay there [Manchester City] for three or four years at the most. He could be, for example, two-and-a-half years in Germany, two-and-a-half years in England and then in Spain, Italy, France, right?"

With the time frame in mind, Haaland Sr believes his son could depart at the end of the current season. The ex-striker even had some clubs in mind, naming six that he thought the Norway international could consider.

‌



He added: "On our list, I think City is the best team. [Bayern] Munich is number two. We have Real Madrid as number three, Paris Saint-Germain as number four.

View 2 Images Haaland could consider leaving City (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

"We also have some English teams other than City who are quite good. Liverpool and Chelsea. Also, there is Barcelona. They are sort of in the same row."

‌



In 2025, Haaland signed a contract extension that ties him to City until 2034. However, Real and Barcelona have both previously eyed the striker and may see the charges as a new incentive to secure his services.

The 26-year-old is yet to address City's verdict, but previously claimed he wants to remain at the club for a long time. Discussing his bumper new contract last year, Haaland said: "It has been amazing, and it's been like a dream these past two and a half years, but I'm really looking forward to what's next and for the future.

"I'm going to stay for a long time so now I can fully focus on getting better because [I know] I'm going to stay for such a long time. So, [the] full focus [is] on performing and getting better and to give all the fans what they want."

Sports.title: Liverpool confirm Alexander Isak injury status after star returns from Sweden duty
Sports.content:
Liverpool confirm Alexander Isak injury status after star returns from Sweden duty

Liverpool striker Alexander Isak scored in Sweden's Nations League victory over Romania but will now return to Anfield earlier than planned after suffering a knock

View 2 Images Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool (Image: Patrick Smith/FIFA)

Liverpool have announced that Alexander Isak has returned early from international duty after sustaining a 'minor injury' during a Sweden game.

‌



The Reds striker scored in a 2-1 win for Graham Potter's team over Romania to continue his prolific start to the season. However, Isak's evening was marred by a stamp which left him with a bloody toe, although he played down the severity of the issue during a post-match conversation with the media.

‌



"You can see it [the injury], "Isak is said to have told reporters. "It was a real stamp. Those of you who have played might know that it takes a few minutes before it lets go, but it was okay."

‌



Though Isak did not seem concerned, it has now been confirmed by Liverpool that he will no longer participate in Sweden's remaining three fixtures during the international break, with Potter later confirming the 27-year-old had a thigh issue.
