World.title: School calendar: When do schools open for Term 4?
World.content:
Public schools across South Africa will reopen for Term 4 on Tuesday, 6 October, according to the Department of Basic Education’s official 2026 school calendar.

Pupils have been on holiday since Term 3 closed on 23 September. The spring break gives families just under two weeks at home before the final stretch of the school year begins.

The date applies to all public schools nationwide, as all nine provinces follow one unified school calendar.



SCHOOL CALENDAR: HOW LONG WILL TERM 4 RUN

Term 4 runs for ten weeks, from 6 October to 9 December, and includes 47 school days.

No public holidays fall during the term, so pupils face ten straight weeks of teaching and assessment.

Schools use this term to finish the curriculum, write final exams, and decide which pupils progress to the next grade. Grade 12 pupils also write their National Senior Certificate exams during this period.



Pupils already enjoyed an extra day off before the break even started. Heritage Day fell on Thursday, 24 September, the day after schools closed.

HOW THE 2026 SCHOOL YEAR STACKS UP

Term 4 is the last of four terms in the 2026 academic year.

Term 1 had 53 school days, Term 2 had 54, and Term 3 had 47. The Department structured the calendar to keep the four terms relatively even, with around 200 official school days across the year.



The calendar also separates school days from other non-teaching days, including weekends, administration days, public holidays and special school holidays.

WHAT PARENTS SHOULD NOTE BEFORE SCHOOLS OPEN

Parents planning trips, medical appointments or other commitments should work from the confirmed 6 October return date. School calendars shift slightly from year to year depending on how public holidays fall, so last year’s dates are not a reliable guide.

With final exams ahead, the remaining holiday days are a good time to check report cards, set study timetables and sort out uniforms and school supplies.



Families with children at independent schools should confirm dates directly with their school, as private schools may follow a different calendar.

World.title: 'Tenders feed corruption', EFF calls for in-sourcing in NMB
World.content:
GQEBERHA - The Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) in Nelson Mandela Bay Municipality are calling for an infrastructure rehabilitation program.

"We have been putting a plaster on a wound," said the party’s NMB mayoral candidate Sinawo Thambo.

Thambo says the City needs a fixed plan that guarantees that water leaks and other municipal damages are fixed timeously.

"The infrastructure has collapsed; it has not been maintained," Thambo explained.

"There is no business that can operate in a City where there's constant water and electricity outages; that is why we are seeing a lot of disinvestment in the City."

Thambo was speaking during eNCA's election roundtable at Nelson Mandela University on Sunday.

Nelson Mandela Bay has one of the highest irregular expenditures of any metro in South Africa. The SIU has revealed a R35 million streetlight scandal, implicating 21 officials.

The Metro has had a revolving door of mayors and city managers since the 2021 local government elections. The City is under financial strain and was one of the municipalities on the list when Treasury withheld equitable share allocations to local governments in July.

The Red Berets are calling for increased state capacity.

"A lot of corruption and irregular expenditures are a result of the City being highly dependent on contracting, like all other municipalities in the country," Thambo says.

"There is a reliance on tendering, and tendering feeds corruption," he adds.

Thambo has called for internal capacity building and in-sourcing.

World.title: "We are not running well at the moment", DA calls for professionalisation of Nelson Mandela Bay
World.content:
GQEBERHA - GQEBERHA - The Nelson Mandela Bay Municipality is not running well 'at the moment,' says the Democratic Alliance's mayoral candidate, Retief Odendaal.

He says service delivery in the municipality has collapsed. He warned about a disinvestment in the City. The DA’s NMB mayoral candidate was speaking during eNCA's election roundtable at Nelson Mandela University on Sunday.

"We need to professionalise the administration," he declared.

"We need to headhunt professional people to return to our administration, engineers, plumbers, electricians, and not people connected to politicians," he added.

Nelson Mandela Bay has one of the highest irregular expenditures of any metro in South Africa. The SIU has revealed a R35 million streetlight scandal, implicating 21 officials.

The Metro has had a revolving door of mayors and city managers since the 2021 local government elections. The City is under financial strain and was one of the municipalities on the list when Treasury withheld equitable share allocations to local governments in July.

Odendaal wants the municipality to address the financial freefall.

"We are going to be bankrupt within a couple of months if it is not immediately addressed," he explained.

World.title: Boks humbled in Perth
World.content:
PERTH - The Wallabies have stunned the Springboks in Perth to claim a memorable 42-38 win over the World Champions.

The Australians started like a house on fire against a Springbok side that had no less than 13 changes to the team that clinched Rugby's Greatest Rivalry two weeks ago.

Les Kiss' side ran in five tries which was enough to hold off the visitors who made a late charge to reduce what was a 25-point deficit.

It will be very little consolation for Rassie Erasmus' team who were playing against an Aussie outfit with just 11-men on the field.

The win also marks the Wallabies second victory over the Boks in their last three encounters.

World.title: Ekurhuleni Murders | 11th woman's body found in Springs
World.content:
SPRINGS - Another woman's body has been found half-naked in Ekurhuleni.

This brings the number of victims found in the area to 11.

Gauteng police spokesperson Brigadier Brenda Muridili said the body was discovered in an open veld near Rhokana Road.

"A security company vehicle patrolling the area noticed the body and alerted the police.

"All necessary role-players have been mobilised, including the Task Team investigating the Ekurhuleni murder cases, Crime Scene Management, Investigative Psychology Services (IPS), Detectives and Crime Intelligence," she said.

This is a developing story.

World.title: Another win for SIU in Tembisa Hospital corruption case
World.content:
THEMBISA - The Special Investigating Unit has secured R42.4million in cash and assets linked to alleged bribes at Tembisa Hospital.

They include properties, pension benefits and investments.

The SIU said the money is linked to businessman Stefan Govindraju's alleged syndicate.

It said the syndicate used 75 companies to secure around R600 million in hospital contracts and R100million was paid to hospital officials as kickbacks.

Govindraju was arrested last month and faces 70 charges linked to the alleged corruption.

The SIU has referred evidence of possible criminal conduct to the NPA and is continuing to recover money the state lost.

World.title: Ramaphosa calls for action against GBV perpetrators
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - President Cyril Ramaphosa has called for greater action against gender-based violence perpetrators.

He has urged communities to confront abuse and hold those responsible to account.

Ramaphosa said the fight against the scourge must start at home.

He was speaking at the Synodal Men's Guild Conference of the Evangelical Presbyterian Church.

"We must refuse to excuse controlling behaviour as love. We must refuse to look away when we know that someone is being abused. We must refuse to protect perpetrators because they are our friends, our relatives, our colleagues or even members of our congregations.

"Silence cannot be our response to violence. For scripture reminds us that faith without works is dead. If we say that we believe in the dignity of every person and human being, then that belief must be visible in the way that we live, in the way that we speak, in the way that we believe, we behave.

"It must be visible in everything that we do. But it must also be visible in the way that we raise our children as well, particularly the boy child. It must be visible in the way that we treat women.

"It must also be visible in the courage with which we confront wrongdoing. Our covenant must also begin in the home. Fathers must understand that their sons are watching them.

World.title: Change South Africa to Azania – ATM president Caesar Nongqunga
World.content:
DURBAN - The name South Africa is just a geographical direction and must be changed.

This is the view of President of the African Transformation Movement, Caesar Nongqunga.

ATM has unveiled its mayoral candidates for the Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal.

It promises to make deeper, meaningful change across the South African political landscape and society.

And contesting the election in all nine provinces on the 4th of November, is a start towards making its presence felt.

For ATM President Caesar Nongqunga, Azania is the ideal name.

"I’m very serious. You know, once you rob a person of his identity, you have committed a crime. You have committed a crime, and that crime is very serious. South Africans need to know who they are. They cannot be named after a location because this thing that says South Africa is just a location.

"If we are able to change the names of towns and airports, why can't we change this one so that we may understand and know who we are? That is all. It will need process. We are the process because we are the people, we are the community, we are the people who are feeling this pain. So, the process has already started by me saying it.”

With the local government polls just over a month away, Nongqunga said his party’s candidates will focus on water supply as their main service delivery priority.

“The first thing that you must be sure of is the provision of water and we have catered for that. The second thing is the infrastructure, and the third thing is to build the capacity to repair or to maintain the infrastructure; those are the things that I think are main. Others will be done because they overlap, trying to make sure that the sport is encouraged in each and every place, especially in towns, townships, and rural areas.”

Nongqunga is not ruling out cooperation with other like-minded parties.

He says the ATM is willing to enter into coalitions in councils where there are no outright winners.

World.title: Bangkok floods send thousands into shelters after days of rain
World.content:
BANGKOK - Deep floodwaters in Bangkok drove thousands of residents into shelters as others scrambled to buy groceries or dry out their homes on Sunday after days of heavy rain inundated markets, roads and residences.

Pedestrians in plastic rain ponchos waded through murky, knee-deep water in the Thai capital, some venturing into a supermarket while others floated their belongings in plastic tubs.

"People cannot get out of their homes. We are running out of food, so I came out to purchase some," Aduenan Surorot, a motorbike-taxi driver, told AFP outside a grocery store.

The shops near his house, where flooding was still at chest level, were low on stock, the 30-year-old said.

He waited about two hours in the cashier's queue, with customers crowded inside but few staff working.

World.title: Kalonzo signals at working with Ruto if 2027 poll is free and fair
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County on September 27, 2026. [Clinton Ambujo, Standard]

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka has signalled that the Opposition could accept the outcome of the 2027 General Election and consider working with President William Ruto if he wins through a free and fair contest.

Speaking at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County, Kalonzo said the political class must commit itself to democratic competition and be prepared to accept the verdict of voters.

“If you beat us, we will have to consider if you have behaved yourself, and if we beat you, we have to look at all these things,” he said.

The Wiper leader also called for stronger democratic institutions, warning against political confrontation that could deepen divisions in the country.

“We have a nation here. We have to make this country truly democratic. I do not think we have a shortcut,” he said.

Kalonzo used the church service to make a broader appeal for a united and effective Opposition, saying political leaders had a responsibility to work together in the national interest.

“Kenya needs a functional official opposition; one that is united and does not thrive on disunity. As leaders, we have a responsibility to work together and play our part in fixing this nation,” he said.

He said he had remained in the Opposition even when some political allies moved into government.

“I have stood in the opposition all these years. Even when others joined government, my brother Eugene Wamalwa and I remained steadfast, and we will continue to stand firm,” he said.

Kalonzo also turned his attention to Parliament, claiming that the National Assembly had been “captured” and challenging lawmakers in both Houses to exercise their constitutional responsibilities.

“The National Assembly has been captured. Let this message reach every leader in the National Assembly and the Senate: you have the power to change things, not just to complain later,” he said.

He urged legislators to defend the interests of the people who elected them and to put the country ahead of political considerations.

The former Vice President also defended retired President Uhuru Kenyatta against claims that he is financing the Opposition ahead of the 2027 contest.

Kalonzo argued that presidential campaigns have historically relied on networks of political allies and supporters rather than family resources alone.

“But here we are saying, please let Uhuru rest; he is a retired President. Stop saying he is our financier,” he said.

Kalonzo cited previous presidential campaigns involving Uhuru, former President Mwai Kibaki and Raila Odinga, arguing that major political campaigns require support from friends and associates.

“Even when Uhuru was running for President, or Kibaki and even Raila, no family has enough resources to support a presidential campaign. It is friends who support you,” he said.

He warned that Kenya was at a delicate political moment and urged leaders to avoid actions that could deepen instability.

“We should not allow the country to get to a worse situation than where it is. We are on the edge of a cliff; the country is at a crossroads,” he said.

World.title: ODM delegates reject Sakaja using the party for gubernatorial bid
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi ODM chairman George Aladwa addressing the media over the upcoming ODM nominations in Nairobi. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

Nairobi ODM delegates have resolved to reject and lobby against attempts by some people in President William Ruto's broad-based government to give Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja the ODM ticket in the 2027 gubernatorial race.

Party members, delegates and branch chairpersons met in Makadara, where they agreed that ODM be allowed to field their own candidates instead of the party allowing UDA leaders to vie on the party ticket.

They also resolved to back Makadara MP George Aladwa. With Tutam songs renting the air during the meeting, they also agreed to back President Ruto's re-election.

"Aladwa should be the party's candidate for Nairobi governor, and every candidate should seek the seat through their own political party," said an agitated delegate from Kasarani.

They insisted ODM should not allow an outsider to join the party and use its ticket to contest for the gubernatorial seat, arguing that the ODM ticket should be reserved for a candidate who enjoys the support of its members.

"We will not allow someone from another party to come and vie using ODM while we have our own members. As a party our only candidate is Aladwa," said delegate chairs.

They added that their position follows a series of meetings held across all 17 constituencies in Nairobi, with Makadara being the final constituency to hold its meeting.

They further argued that the Nairobi gubernatorial seat requires a leader with experience and leadership skills, warning ODM members against supporting candidates they believe lack the necessary political and leadership experience.

They also sustained their criticism towards former president Uhuru, alleging that he is undermining the party and dividing it, and they will not allow it.

George Aladwa backed the ODM members' position, saying every politician seeking elective office should do so through their own political party.

The delegates maintained that ODM should protect its identity and ticket, insisting that candidates from outside the party should not be allowed to use the ODM ticket to pursue elective positions when active and loyal members are sidelined.

The delegates are calling on ODM to ensure that the nomination process is free, fair and transparent, giving party members an opportunity to choose the candidate they want to represent them.

World.title: Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya's first commercial drilling
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya’s first commercial drilling. [Courtes]

Kenya has moved closer to commercial oil production after a 1,500 horsepower drilling rig arrived at the Port of Mombasa ahead of its deployment to the South Lokichar Basin in Turkana County.

The GW70 rig, leased by Gulf Energy E&P BV from Great Wall Drilling Company, docked at Kilindini Port on Friday aboard MV Transit Sedanka after sailing from Duqm Port in Oman.

It is expected to be transported to Turkana, where drilling is scheduled to begin on November 1.

“All workstreams at Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ are running to a tight project management schedule, and the project remains on course for First Oil production in December 2026,” Gulf Energy Chief Executive Officer Paul Limoh said.

The arrival marks a step in the commercial development of the South Lokichar Basin, more than a decade after oil was first discovered in Turkana in 2012.

The first phase of the project is expected to produce about 20,000 barrels of crude oil per day, with output projected to rise to 50,000 barrels per day in the second phase.

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) says Kenya is targeting first oil in December 2026, while the first crude exports through the Port of Mombasa are expected in the first quarter of 2027.

The GW70 will undergo commissioning and acceptance checks before drilling begins. Gulf Energy has contracted Baker Hughes for integrated well services and SLB to provide an early production facility for the first phase.

World.title: Two more suspects arrested over lawyer Kyalo Mbobu murder
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads.

Detectives have arrested two more suspects in connection with the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu, as an intelligence-led operation targeting people linked to the September 9, 2025 murder intensifies.

The two boda boda riders Nicholas Lemiso Naula and Noah Kipkirui Langat were arrested in Nairobi’s Central Business District, following sustained efforts by detectives to trace individuals suspected to have been involved in the killing.

According to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Lemiso is a boda boda rider who allegedly ferried the main suspect, Police Constable Julius Cheruiyot, to and from the scene of the murder, while Langat was arrested over alleged surveillance on Mbobu before his killing.

"With three suspects now in custody, detectives are intensifying the hunt for other persons suspected to have played a role in the meticulously planned killing," DCI stated.

His arrest comes shortly after detectives arrested Cheruiyot in connection with the killing.

“The dragnet over the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu has widened, with detectives arresting a second suspect as an intelligence-led operation targeting persons linked to the murder intensifies,” DCI said.

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads and seek to identify and arrest other people who may have been involved. The DCI said the operation remains active as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding Mbobu’s murder.

“The DCI is leaving no stone unturned in its efforts to unravel the full circumstances surrounding Lawyer Mbobu’s murder and bring all those responsible to justice,” the agency said.

World.title: KRA seizes 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret Airport
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The consignment was intercepted by KRA enforcement teams following an intelligence report.

Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has seized a consignment containing 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret International Airport, averting a potential tax loss of Sh21.5 million.

KRA enforcement teams intercepted the consignment after an intelligence report indicated it contained undeclared mobile phones and other high-end electronic goods.

The cargo, which had been declared under five Customs entries, was part of consolidated shipments that also included shoes, clothing, automotive spare parts, household goods, electronic accessories and other assorted items.

KRA said an initial declaration listed only 3,000 smartphones. However, verification established 55,607 ordinary smartphones, alongside 309 undeclared high-end smartphones.

The high-end devices included Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Samsung Galaxy Z Fold and Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max models.

“The consignment therefore reflects both under-declaration and non-declaration of dutiable goods,” KRA said in a statement issued on Wednesday.

The tax authority said the verification exercise was conducted to establish whether all mobile phones contained in the consignment had been properly declared.

KRA said the alleged tax evasion contravenes Section 203 of the East African Community Customs Management Act (EACCMA), 2004.

The law provides that a person who makes a false or incorrect Customs entry, or knowingly participates in the fraudulent evasion of duty, commits an offence.

“A person who, in any matter relating to Customs, makes any entry which is false or incorrect in any particular, or in any way is knowingly concerned in any fraudulent evasion of the payment of any duty, commits an offence,” KRA said, citing the law.

According to the authority, a person convicted under the provision is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or a fine of up to US$10,000.

KRA said it was intensifying efforts to uncover tax evasion schemes to improve revenue compliance and ensure adherence to tax laws and procedures.

“KRA is actively engaged in unearthing tax evasion schemes to boost tax revenue compliance as well as adherence to tax laws and procedures, hence ensuring fair trade is maintained within the market,” the authority said.

The authority also appealed to members of the public, taxpayers and businesses with information on individuals, companies or networks involved in the generation, sale, purchase or use of fictitious VAT invoices to report them.

KRA said information provided would be treated confidentially and the identity of informants kept anonymous.

World.title: 'We know what happened': Uhuru claims Raila won 2022 polls
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta. [File, Standard]

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta says he remains convinced that Raila Odinga won the 2022 presidential election.

Speaking during a Jubilee Party meeting in Nairobi on Tuesday, September 22, Uhuru questioned how the Azimio coalition could have lost the presidency despite performing strongly in other elective races.

“We did everything to help Baba become President of the Republic of Kenya. He got the votes, and to this day I know that he is the one who won those votes. We know how things happened, and we do not want it to happen that way again,” Uhuru said.

The late Odinga contested the August 9, 2022 election under the Azimio la Umoja-One Kenya Coalition Party, with Martha Karua as his running mate. Ruto ran under the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) as the presidential candidate of the Kenya Kwanza Alliance.

Ruto was declared president-elect after garnering 7,176,141 votes, 50.49 per cent, against Odinga's 6,942,930 votes, 48.85 per cent. Ruto's margin was 233,211 votes.

The Supreme Court later unanimously upheld his election after dismissing petitions challenging the results.

But Uhuru pointed to the coalition's performance in the parliamentary and county races to question how Azimio could have lost the presidency.

“How can you say we were defeated when we had most of the MPs, governors and senators? How were we defeated in the presidency?” he asked.

In the National Assembly, figures published after the election initially put Azimio ahead of Kenya Kwanza, with 165 seats against 160, while 12 seats were held by independent MPs.

Azimio also won 23 of the 47 governorships, while Kenya Kwanza secured 22. The remaining two were won by Taita Taveta Governor Andrew Mwadime and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza, who ran as independent candidates.

In the Senate, Kenya Kwanza had an advantage, winning 24 of the 47 directly elected seats against Azimio's 23.

The parliamentary balance later shifted in favour of Kenya Kwanza after several MPs changed their political allegiance.

In October 2022, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula declared Kenya Kwanza the majority coalition with 179 MPs against Azimio's 157, after several MPs from parties including UDM, MDG, Maendeleo Chap Chap and PAA moved towards the Kenya Kwanza side.

Uhuru also rejected claims that he was responsible for Odinga's loss, saying he was not a candidate in the election.

“I am surprised when people say that we did not help Baba and that they defeated me. I was not on the ballot, and they are lying. I was only Raila's handyman,” he said.

He warned against what he described as divisive and dirty politics, saying Kenya should not repeat the events surrounding the 2022 election.

“Dirty politics and politics aimed at dividing Kenyans will take us nowhere. Let us not divide each other. What does it help us? Sell your manifesto,” Uhuru said.

He said he accepted the Supreme Court's decision after the 2022 presidential petitions and handed over power to Ruto without disputing the outcome, accusing Ruto of dragging his name in his failed leadership.

“When we finished and the court ruled, we did not dispute it. We went and handed over the presidency to them. And now, after four years, they are still talking about Uhuru. But when things are not working, people tend to look for excuses,” he said.

This is the clearest public assertion by the former president since the 2022 elections that Odinga won the presidential vote.

World.title: Ruto offers Kenya as test case on African risk
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto with Dangote Industries President and CEO Aliko Dangote and Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) CEO Samaila Zubairu on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, USA. [PCS]

President William Ruto has offered Kenya as a test case for how African risk is assessed, saying the country will open its default and recovery data to rating agencies and accept changes to the methodology if the evidence supports them.

Ruto said financial rules are steering African pension savings towards government securities rather than infrastructure, even where regulations allow greater investment in projects.

He made the proposal Monday, September 21, at the Africa We Build High-Level Roundtable on regulation, risk and reward in New York. The Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) convened the event on the margins of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Kenyan pension funds hold 46 per cent of their Sh3.2 trillion ($24.7 billion) in government securities but only 0.02 per cent in infrastructure debt, Ruto said. The rules allow pension funds to invest up to 10 per cent in infrastructure.

“Africa's problem is no longer the amount of capital available to it. Africa's problem is the set of rules that decide where that capital is allowed to go,” Ruto noted.

Ruto returned to an argument he made at the inaugural Africa We Build Summit in Nairobi in April, where he said African countries should use domestic capital to finance their own infrastructure.

At the New York roundtable, he revisited his earlier phrase, “he who pays the piper calls the tune”, using a teacher in Eldoret who has contributed to a pension fund for 20 years to illustrate his point.

“In Nairobi I said that he who pays the piper calls the tune. I meant it as a warning about depending on other people's money. This morning I mean it as an opportunity. The teacher in Eldoret is paying the piper. She has earned the right to call the tune,” Ruto explained.

He said the teacher's savings are more likely to sit in a US Treasury bill than in a nearby geothermal plant.

“Her fund manager is not being unpatriotic. He is being rational. The rules he works under tell him the Treasury bill is prudent and the power plant is adventurous. Capital follows incentives, and we wrote the incentives,” Ruto observed.

The Africa Finance Corporation's President and Chief Executive Samaila Zubairu framed the wider problem in similar terms at the Nairobi summit, saying Africa is “not capital-poor; it is capital-trapped.”

Ruto now wants African risk assessed using evidence from African markets rather than assumptions that he argues can make projects and countries appear more expensive to finance.

He said Kenya will make its pension and insurance regulators available to work with rating agencies, insurers and standard setters.

“If the evidence vindicates the current methodology, we will accept the finding and say so publicly. If it does not, we will expect the methodology to change,” Ruto added.

He proposed that the roundtable establish a working group based in Nairobi to continue the work and report to the next Africa We Build Summit in 12 months with findings backed by numbers.

President William Ruto on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, USA. [PCS]

Ruto made four requests to rating agencies, insurers, regulators and other institutions involved in financing: price African risk against African experience, make insurance on productive assets affordable, end penalties on long-term assets in prudential and liquidity rules and build bankable project pipelines.

He said African non-bank domestic capital pools have passed $2 trillion, while external concessional and commercial flows to Africa totalled $1.7 trillion between 2014 and 2024.

Official development assistance has also fallen every year since 2020, Ruto said, arguing that Africa can no longer rely on external financing to meet its infrastructure needs.

Kenya has begun putting some of the proposed financing mechanisms in place.

Ruto said the National Infrastructure Fund, signed into law in March, aims to mobilise up to $40 billion for roads, ports, power and water without new public debt.

In May, Kenya listed its first infrastructure fund on the Nairobi Securities Exchange and raised Sh3.4 billion with United Kingdom support. Kenya also increased its equity in the Africa Finance Corporation by Sh3.25 billion ($25 million), Ruto said.

The president said Kenya was willing to expose its own financing system to scrutiny as part of the test.

“If the evidence supports the current methodology, we will accept it. If it does not, we will expect the methodology to change,” Ruto told the roundtable.

The broader goal, he said, is to make it as easy for African institutional investors to finance productive assets as it is to buy government debt.

“The day a Kenyan pension trustee can buy a Kenyan power station as easily as she buys a Treasury bill, this argument will be over,” Ruto said.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro, Kinangop MP clash over alleged threatening message
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro arrives at St Paul ACK church in Engineer Town for the service on September 20, 2026. [James Munyeki, Standard]

There was drama at St Paul ACK church in Engineer Town during service on Sunday after Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro clashed with Kinangop MP Zachary Kwenya Thuku over an alleged threatening message.

Thuku, who is allied to the Kenya Kwanza government led by President William Ruto, is said to have warned Nyoro against attending the service.

"Yesterday, I received a message from the MP for Kinangop, Kwenya Thuku, warning me not to attend the church service. If I am lying, let him come here and read the message he sent me," Nyoro said.

He challenged the Kinangop MP to read the message aloud to the congregation.

"If anything happens to me today, Kenyans will judge whoever will be responsible," said Nyoro.

The Kiharu MP challenged Thuku to face him at a public rally at Engineer Trading Centre.

When he rose to speak, the Kinangop MP said he would not address the matter in church.

Instead, he said this was a political issue that the leaders would resolve.

"Let us solve this matter amicably. We are all brothers in this political journey," he said amid cheers from the congregation.

Recently, Nyoro added his voice to the growing political realignment in Mt Kenya, openly acknowledging the political tightrope he now walks as he distances himself from his former allies in the ruling party.

In a candid interview, he admitted that his previous close ties with President William Ruto and the Kenya Kwanza administration have left him vulnerable to suspicion from both sides of the political divide but insisted his decision to abandon the ruling party, United Democratic Alliance (UDA) was deliberate, difficult, and necessary.

World.title: South Africa police hunt suspects after three shootings leave more than 30 people dead
World.content:
Police are hunting for suspects after three separate shootings overnight in South Africa left more than 30 people dead, as the country grapples with a spate of violent crime.

South African police launched a manhunt Sunday after 17 people were killed and 15 wounded in a shooting in the township of Wedela in West Rand District outside Johannesburg.

Police said eight unidentified men opened fire on patrons drinking outside a tavern on Saturday evening local time, before they entered the establishment and “continued shooting at patrons inside.”

The alleged assailants were reportedly armed with pistols and AK-47 rifles, officers said.

“It is alleged that patrons were drinking inside and outside the tavern when the suspects arrived and opened fire on those outside. The suspects then entered the tavern and continued shooting at patrons inside,” South Africa police wrote on X. The attackers allegedly searched some patrons and took their cellphones before fleeing the scene in two unidentified motor vehicles.

Separately, 10 people were shot and killed at an entertainment venue in Lwandle, a township in the Western Cape, South Africa, early Sunday morning, police said.

Police reports indicate that gunmen entered early on Sunday local time and fired at patrons. Five people died at the scene while five others succumbed to their injuries in hospital.

A manhunt to find the suspects has been launched. No arrests have yet been made, according to police.

The police commissioner said a business dispute was a possible motive.

“It seems that there’s business rivalry, business jealousy that might have been there the issue because of the people are buying alcohol maybe at cheaper places and they come and drink in this place. But we are still investigating that.” Lieutenant General Sizkhele William Dyantyi said.

Also in Western Cape, police said they are investigating a quadruple murder following a shooting incident in the township of Khayelitsha at approximately 7.15 p.m. Saturday evening.

Three men with multiple gunshot wounds were found at the scene. Two of the victims were discovered inside a vehicle, while the third victim was found next to the vehicle. They were declared deceased at the scene, police said.

A fourth victim was who had also sustained gunshot wounds was taken to a medical facility but succumbed to his injuries upon arrival, according to the police statement.

A suspect has not yet been identified or arrested, and police have not yet established a motive.

Crime on the rise

While violent crime has been a long-standing issue in South Africa, experts say that the rate of mass shootings is on the rise. They often impact people from the country’s poorest communities.

Last week 11 people, including a woman believed to be pregnant, were killed when gunmen opened fire at a house south of the city of Durban.

The latest police figures show that an average of 58 people were murdered each day in South Africa between January and March.

The violence has also left women particularly fearful. In recent weeks, the discovery of the bodies of 10 women in parts of Johannesburg, the country’s largest city, has caused widespread alarm. Several of the bodies were found near roads or in open areas, and police are investigating whether some of the deaths are connected.

South Africa is also battling powerful criminal networks involved in drugs, extortion, illegal mining and gang violence. The 2025 Africa Organized Crime Index says cocaine from South America passes through the country on its way to other parts of the world.

Organized crime has also become an issue within the country’s police leadership. Police minister Senzo Mchunu was placed on leave last year after accusations that he had links to a criminal syndicate and interfered with police investigations. He has denied the allegations.

President Cyril Ramaphosa said in February that organized crime was “the most immediate threat to our democracy, our society and our economic development.”

Ramaphosa announced that soldiers would be deployed to support police in tackling gang violence, as the government steps up its fight against criminal syndicates.

This story has been updated with new developments.

Nimi Princewill contributed reporting.

World.title: Deluge begins in Hawaii as Hurricane Nolo continues to strengthen
World.content:
Heavy rain from Hurricane Nolo is ramping up in southern Hawaii, the islands’ third dangerous brush with a hurricane in just six weeks. Potentially life-threatening flooding and mudslides are again possible as the state contends with a Pacific tropical season supercharged by this year’s super El Niño.

Nolo rapidly intensified into a Category 2 hurricane Friday and remained at that strength on Saturday morning. Rapid intensification is an increase in maximum sustained wind speeds of at least 35 mph in 24 hours or less, and it’s happening more frequently in a world warming due to fossil fuel pollution.

The Big Island will see the worst of Nolo’s impacts as it continues to strengthen and makes its closest approach Saturday local time. Extreme rain is its most serious threat, but Nolo is also whipping up strong wind gusts and dangerous seas.

Hurricane Lala took a similarly close track to the Big Island in mid-August as a Category 1 storm and unleashed catastrophic flooding there. On the other side of the state, Hurricane Lowell delivered a blow to Kauai and Niihau in early September as a Category 2 storm.

Hawaii Gov. Josh Green has declared a state of emergency, the third storm-related emergency declaration this month, in anticipation of the storm’s impacts. And President Donald Trump approved the state’s request for a pre-landfall Presidential Emergency Declaration, Green said Friday.

Flooding rain, mudslides possible

Nolo is expected to make its closest approach to the Big Island as a high-end Category 2 hurricane or a Category 3 major hurricane.

Nolo’s rainbands continue to spin into the Big Island and they will spread to Maui, Lanai and Molokai on Saturday.

Rainfall totals have lowered with the most recent forecast, but a dangerous amount is still possible.

Eight to 12 inches of rain are possible over eastern and southern portions of the Big Island through Sunday, with up to 16 inches in the steepest terrain, according to the National Hurricane Center. Last month, the Big Island’s steep mountains helped wring more than 40 inches of rain out of Hurricane Lala’s bands, unleashing catastrophic flash flooding from which the island is still recovering.

Rainfall forecast this weekend. CNN Weather

Nolo’s rainfall is expected to be lower, but still significant on the western side of the island, with up to 6 inches possible.

In eastern Maui, 4 to 6 inches are possible with isolated amounts up to 8 inches. About 1 to 3 inches of rain are expected elsewhere on the main islands.

Nolo’s strongest winds will remain offshore since the hurricane is passing well to the south of the Big Island. Still, tropical storm-force winds stronger than 40 mph are likely in areas of steep terrain on Saturday and hurricane-force gusts stronger than 75 mph can’t be ruled out.

Hawaii battens down — again

State and county offices, public schools and the University of Hawaii are closed Thursday and Friday on the Big Island and will close Friday on Maui, Gov. Green said in a social media post.

Approximately 400 National Guard troops are positioned across the state, with 121 on the Big Island, the governor said in an update Friday.

County officials have opened shelters on the Big Island. “If your home flooded before, or is at risk, consider moving to safer shelter before the full force of the storm hits,” Hawaii County Mayor Kimo Alameda said in a Wednesday news release. “Because the ground remains saturated, flooding may happen rapidly.”

The state has also secured 100 hotel rooms for Big Island residents who wish to evacuate, Green said at a Wednesday news conference. Statewide, hundreds of people are still being housed in hotels after being displaced by earlier natural disasters, including hurricanes Lala and Lowell, Department of Human Services director Joseph Campos said at the same conference.

Darren Montalvo loads sand bags into the bed of his truck in Hilo, Hawaii, on Friday. Gregory Bull/AP

On Maui, officials have been preparing emergency generators and storm response equipment, and increasing staffing at police and fire departments, the county said in a social media post. Bus service will be suspended at different points through the weekend.

Offshore, dangerous seas will build and reach their peak Friday and Saturday. Rough conditions will likely last through the weekend and into next week even as the hurricane starts to track west away from the island Sunday night into Monday.

Super El Niño’s dominance

This year’s super El Nino has helped prime the Pacific to be a factory for strong tropical systems, with extremely warm ocean water and a lack of storm-killing wind shear.

Nolo is one of 19 named storms — including three Category 5 hurricanes — that have roamed the eastern and central Pacific so far and there are two full months of the season left to go. Seventeen originated in the eastern Pacific basin, which typically sees up to 15 storms in an entire season.

For the second time this month, a trio of hurricanes — Nolo, Odalys and Polo — are simultaneously churning in the Pacific.

Polo, which is still roaring off the coast of southern Mexico, is one of five storms this season that have met the criteria for extreme rapid intensification, a wind increase of 58 mph or more in 24 hours.

World.title: Three countries open their doors to Egyptians with financial grants and housing
World.content:
Several countries have begun offering direct financial incentives to encourage citizens and eligible foreign nationals to relocate to small villages and islands facing depopulation.

These incentives take various forms, including assistance with home purchases, grants for remote workers, and programs targeting entrepreneurs and startups.

However, receiving a grant or financial support does not automatically confer the right of residence, as visas, residence permits, and immigration requirements remain subject to the specific laws of each country.

Italy

Italy is offering home purchases in the island of Sardinia, with various local initiatives aimed at attracting residents to its towns and small villages.

Notable examples include programs implemented on Sardinia that target individuals wishing to buy or renovate a home to serve as their primary residence; financial contributions can cover up to 50 percent of eligible expenses, with a maximum cap of €15,000 per beneficiary or household.

Ireland

Ireland is offering grants for the renovation of vacant properties on its islands.

Available incentives include support for the repair and refurbishment of uninhabited properties, with grants reaching up to €60,000.

For abandoned properties, the funding limit may rise to €84,000, including an additional allowance to offset the higher construction costs associated with island locations.

Switzerland

The Swiss village of Albinen offers incentives linked to the purchase or investment of a property that meets specific criteria; however, benefiting from these incentives entails a long-term residency commitment.

The program requires an investment of at least 200,000 Swiss francs (approximately $248,000) and a 10-year residency period.

This does not automatically grant foreigners the right to immigrate, as obtaining residency remains subject to Swiss regulations, particularly for citizens of countries outside the European Union and the European Economic Area.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Germany’s AfD is so extreme it’s putting off other far-right parties
World.content:
The rise of Germany’s Alternative for Germany (AfD) is causing widespread alarm, including in unexpected quarters – other far-right European parties.

While the German party is winning record levels of support at home, some of its closest ideological allies elsewhere in Europe are keeping it at arm’s length.

That tension was again on display after Germany’s recent state elections. In the state of Saxony-Anhalt earlier this month, the AfD made historic gains when it won 43.8% of the vote, falling just three seats short of an outright majority. Elections in Mecklenburg- Vorpommern and Berlin last weekend also showed a exodus from mainstream parties to the fringes, notably the AfD.

Several of the bloc’s far-right party leaders have offered their congratulations, including Geert Wilder of the Netherlands’ Party for Freedom, Viktor Orbàn of Hungary’s Fidesz and Santiago Abascal of Spain’s Vox, who hailed the AfD’s advance as “a “great hope for Germany and Europe.”

But some of Europe’s biggest far-right parties – including in France, Italy and Britain – have been silent.

France’s National Rally (RN), once one of the AfD’s closest partners, said even before the Saxony-Anhalt vote that renewed cooperation with the AfD was “not planned.”

For party leader Marine Le Pen, there is a domestic calculation in play as well as an ideological one.

Under her leadership, the National Rally has embraced what it calls “detoxification”, shifting the party away from the overt xenophobia of its roots under her father, Jean-Marie Le Pen, toward the political mainstream.

Softer rhetoric

She has also worked to move the party’s brand away from the stain of two of its founders’ Nazi past. Its anti-immigration rhetoric is softer, its doors open to mixed-race citizens that her father’s generation might not have welcomed as the “right kind” of French. Since Hamas’ October 7 attacks against Israel, she’s made condemning antisemitism a powerful arm in her rebranding.

The RN, in its previous guise as the National Front, had long been a collaborator with the AfD in the European Parliament. But comments from a senior AfD figure talking down the criminal role of Hitler’s SS paramilitary group in World War II as well as the emergence of a secret plan by the German party to expel people of foreign origin en masse crossed the RN’s red lines. An alliance with the AfD wasn’t compatible with the RN’s new image. In May 2024, the French party broke ranks and ties with the German far right.

Marine Le Pen, the president of the Rassemblement National (RN) group in France, shown on September 13, is one of several European far-right figures who have recently denounced the AfD. Thomas Samson/AFP/Getty Images

The split was evident following the AfD’s recent successes, with the RN’s top leadership notably silent. With the 2027 presidential election on the horizon – Marine Le Pen’s best chance yet to win the Elysée Palace – that’s likely a strategy to avoid any negative blowback.

“We have real problems on both style and substance. We do not consider them to be our allies in Germany,” RN lawmaker Franck Allisio told television channel LCI on September 6, the day of the Saxony-Anhalt vote.

‘Extremist’ label

In comparison to the RN, the AfD has made no effort to purge itself of its extremist factions despite now also appealing to a wide range of voters, said Grégoire Roos, director of the Europe, Russia and Eurasia programs at the Chatham House think tank. The AfD has rejected accusations of right-wing extremism, with the party’s co-leaders previously describing Germany’s domestic intelligence agency’s classification of it as “extremist” as an attempt to “distort democratic competition.”

“Unlike the National Rally that has worked extremely hard to wipe out any morally disturbing elements… the AfD hasn’t conducted such a clean-up,” Roos told CNN.

Figures within the AfD are also comfortable talking about the Nazi era as though not everything from that period of history should be “thrown in the garbage,” another aspect which makes the party unpalatable to most of its European peers, Roos said.

Several AfD members seated at the Federal Press Conference in Berlin on Monday. The party has sought to rebuff the Germany domestic intelligence agency’s “extremist” classification. Sebastian Gollnow/dpa/AP

The more radical far-right French party of Éric Zemmour, Reconquest, however, welcomed the AfD’s win in Saxony-Anhalt. Leading Reconquest MEP Sarah Knafo called the results “historic” in an election night X post. “The European peoples have shown a great deal of patience. Today, they want to take their destiny back into their own hands. An entire continent is rising up,” she said.

In this vein, the AfD is not completely alone. It helped create the Europe of Sovereign Nations group in the European Parliament after its expulsion from Identity and Democracy. The smaller, more isolated group includes nationalist parties such as Reconquest, as well as Bulgaria’s Revival, Hungary’s Our Homeland Movement, Poland’s New Hope and Slovakia’s Republic Movement.

Meloni keeps her distance

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, pictured in Bari, Italy, on September 4, has also cleaved from the AfD, instead hoping to situate her Brothers of Italy party into the political mainstream. Remo Casilli/Reuters

The far-right Brothers of Italy has also not embraced the AfD, with party leader Giorgia Meloni, the Italian prime minister, instead pursuing a strategy of building influence within Europe’s political mainstream.

Her party sits in the European Conservatives and Reformists group, which is more integrated into the European Parliament’s institutional mainstream than the AfD’s Europe of Sovereign Nations grouping. The two parties have deep foreign policy disagreements, with Meloni’s party supporting NATO and Ukraine, while the AfD advocates against sending weapons to Ukraine and wants to lift sanctions on Russia. Meloni has called these differences “irreconcilable.”

Nigel Farage, who spearheads Britain’s hard-right Reform UK party, has described the AfD as a “mixed bag.”

Asked on a podcast with Axel Springer CEO Mathias Döpfner in April what his party’s main differences with the AfD are, Farage said, “I think the pro-Putin stuff, I find it hard to understand.” The AfD’s ties to some dictators were “very, very difficult,” he added.

The AfD’s foreign policy positions have made it an awkward partner for many.

The party contains competing currents over Germany’s relationship with Russia and the US, while its support for closer relations with Moscow separates it from other European right-wing parties. It has also adopted a strong anti-aid rhetoric regarding Ukraine, setting it apart from some, although not all, of Europe’s populist parties.

The party is “very much radical when it comes to Ukraine and Russia,” Roos believes. “Listening to the AfD, you would almost feel like Russia has not invaded Ukraine, that Russia is not committing crimes every single day in Ukraine or killing civilians.” Russia has repeatedly denied accusations of targeting civilians in Ukraine.

Foreign influence

Additionally, parties such as France’s RN have made efforts to disassociate themselves from foreign powers such as Russia and China, while the AfD has not. Last year, the AfD’s links to Beijing were thrust into the spotlight when a former top party aide was convicted in Germany of spying for China.

The AfD has also courted support in Washington. President Donald Trump took to social media to congratulate the party on its landslide victory in Saxony-Anhalt, ending his message with a German variant of his Make America Great Again acronym, “MGGA!”

Elon Musk, who has championed the AfD for years, also expressed his delight.

Elon Musk is seen on a large screen as a previous AfD election party in late January. The US tech billionaire and businessman applauded the group’s gains at recent state elections. AFP/Getty Images

The AfD has maintained a “strong association with Trump and the MAGA movement, which in France, like many European countries, has become increasingly unpopular,” Roos said.

Hypothetically, if the AfD were to make significant regional gains in Germany, it would likely push for a strong nationalist agenda as well as for strengthening relations with Moscow and the lifting of Russian oil and gas sanctions at the European level, Roos said. He pointed out, though, that German foreign policy is vested in the Chancellor’s office, which may limit sudden shifts even if regional support for the AfD’s positions grows.

He added that German democracy remains solid due to its independent judiciary and constitutional court, designed to keep political power in check.

The AfD’s growing strength presents Europe’s far right with a dilemma. If the party continues to gain popularity in Germany, ignoring it could become more complicated. But embracing it could carry political costs for far-right parties that want to demonstrate that they can move from the political margins into government.

World.title: Rogue OpenAI agents targeted three separate US government websites
World.content:
OpenAI said Friday that some of its AI agents went rogue and probed US government websites this summer — the latest revelation of the artificial intelligence company’s technology.

The New York Times first reported that the AI agents went rogue and attempted to gain access to the Education Department, the Commerce Department and the Securities and Exchange Commission, according to security researchers at AI research lab Transluce.

OpenAI said Saturday that its agents accessed publicly available data from the Commerce Department’s Census Bureau using login credentials it found online, and separately shared public data from the SEC website on another website. OpenAI’s agents attempted but failed to gain access to the Education Department and gather data from its civil rights office, according to the report.

OpenAI told CNN in an email that it notified the agencies of the findings while continuing an “extensive review of misaligned model activity.”

“Most of the activity we’ve reviewed so far involved routine research tasks, such as accessing public web content to answer questions. Some involved government websites because our models often turn to them as authoritative sources of public information,” the spokesperson said.

The Commerce Department, SEC and Education Department did not immediately respond to CNN’s requests for comment.

Rep. Jay Obernolte, the Republican co-chair of the AI caucus, told CNN’s Anderson Cooper on Friday that the incident is “another example of a loss of human control.”

“We need to align the values that these models are trained on with human values, and if we can do that, we can get these models to conform to our standards for human behavior,” he said.

The report comes just days after Australia’s prime minister said that an OpenAI agent hacked into the country’s national healthcare database, marking the first known case of AI hacking a government network. Transluce on Wednesday said that it had detected AI agents going rogue dating back to at least March, unsuccessfully targeting a University of New Mexico library and the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare site.

The Australian website probe occurred in June, an OpenAI spokesperson previously told CNN, but the company was only made aware of it in August.

OpenAI has been investigating agents’ use of internet access since the breach of AI start-up Hugging Face in July.

Sam Altman, OpenAI’s chief executive, said Friday on social media site X that the company was not “as fast as we would have liked.”

“We are trying to balance our desire for transparency with gaining a clear understanding … Hugging Face is still the most severe event we’ve seen,” he wrote.

Competitors Anthropic, Meta and Google have also reported that their agents have gone rogue during breach attempts.

Such breaches have raised alarms within the artificial intelligence community. Tech leaders have jointly called for a slowdown of the technology’s development following Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s essay about “pacing the frontier” in mid-September. Amodei warned that people may lose control of AI, which could be misused for “cyberattacks and bioterrorism.”

During the United Nations’ General Assembly on Wednesday, Amodei and Altman urged the UN Security Council to set international standards. Altman said countries need accurate and speedy reporting so that the “world can learn from failures before they become catastrophes.”

Amodei’s warning followed a former Anthropic researcher, Jacob Coxon, whose viral post on X called out AI companies for not acting responsibly with the technology’s development and warned that it “will kill us all.”

AI “doomerism” has faced pushback from tech leaders like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who said there’s a “0% chance” of the world coming to an end in 2030.

World.title: FM hails Egypt-Japan University as model of education cooperation
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty said on Saturday, September 26, 2026, that the Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology (E-JUST) remains a central part of educational cooperation between Egypt and Japan.

These remarks were made in a recorded video address during a ceremony marking the graduation of E-JUST’s 2025 and 2026 classes in Alexandria.

The Minister stated that the university has become one of the main areas of bilateral cooperation, helping train skilled professionals, transfer modern technology, and strengthen educational and scientific ties between the two countries.

Abdelatty affirmed that education is an important part of Egypt-Japan relations, pointing to cooperation between Cairo and Tokyo to establish more than 100 Japanese schools in Egypt.

He also thanked Japan for its support for educational cooperation and praised E-JUST for providing postgraduate scholarships to students from African countries.

The Minister congratulated the graduates, saying their knowledge and technological skills would contribute to Egypt’s development.

President of Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology‏ Ahmed el Sabbagh said that E-JUST is working to prepare graduates for changes in technology, artificial intelligence and the knowledge economy.

He added that the university continues to develop its academic and research programs and expand cooperation with academic and industrial institutions in Egypt and Japan.

The ceremony was attended by Alexandria Governor Ayman Attia, Japanese Ambassador to Egypt Iwai Fumio and the ambassadors of Kenya and Malawi, along with university and education officials.

World.title: Textile industry capable of integrating into global supply chains
World.content:
The Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem said that the textile and spinning sector is a key target of Egypt’s industrial strategy, given its strong potential to integrate into global supply chains, deepen local manufacturing and boost exports.

During a tour of the 6th of October City’s industrial zone, Hashem inspected two factories specialized in textiles, knitting, dyeing, printing and finishing, reviewing production operations and manufacturing stages.

He highlighted the sector’s competitive advantages, including its labor-intensive nature, relatively low energy consumption and availability of skilled workers, which he said could attract further investment and support production and exports.

At Naga Tex, the Minister reviewed a factory producing around 1.44 million meters of fabric annually, with 90 percent local components. The company exports about 60 percent of its output to Switzerland, Turkey, Germany, Brazil and Italy, generating around $2 million in exports.

He also inspected Misr al-Salam for knitting, dyeing, printing and finishing, which has an annual capacity of 5,000 tons of dyed and printed fabric, with 80 percent local components. The company exports 20 percent of its output to Turkey and Morocco, generating three million dollars in exports.

Hashem stressed the importance of raising local components and integrating production chains to enhance the competitiveness of Egyptian products and support the country’s export and industrialization targets.

World.title: Egyptian talent key to attracting global companies to Egypt
World.content:
Ahmed al-Zaher, CEO of the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA), said Egyptian talent is the key factor driving global technology companies to choose Egypt for expansion and international service centers.

Speaking at the ninth edition of DevOpsDays Cairo 2026, El Zaher said rapid advances in artificial intelligence, particularly Agentic AI, are reshaping software development and operations, requiring updated work methodologies, governance and security frameworks, and continued investment in specialized skills.

He highlighted ITIDA’s role, through its Software Engineering Competence Center (SECC), in developing Egyptian capabilities through specialized training, consulting, technical capacity building, and international certifications, enhancing the competitiveness of Egyptian engineers and companies in global markets.

El Zaher said global companies have repeatedly highlighted the quality of Egyptian talent in their meetings with ITIDA, citing a recent meeting with NVIDIA, which expressed appreciation for Egyptian developers and startup founders. NVIDIA’s programs include more than 200 Egyptian startups and around 46,000 programmers, he said.

He added that continued expansion by global companies in Egypt to serve international markets reflects growing confidence in Egyptian talent and strengthens the country’s position as a global technology and digital-services hub.

Held under the theme “Sustainable DevOps in the Agentic AI Era,” the conference brought together local and international experts to discuss AI, cloud computing, cybersecurity and the future of software development and operations. The ninth edition featured 66 speakers, including 13 international speakers from nine countries.

ITIDA has hosted DevOpsDays Cairo since 2018, making Cairo the only Arab city to host the conference, which is held in more than 60 cities worldwide.

World.title: NAPSA urges public to embrace supplementary savings product
World.content:
National Pension Scheme Authority (NAPSA) Chief Executive officer, Muyangwa Muyangwa has called on members of the public to take advantage of a new product introduced by the institution, called Supplementary Savings, to build their wealth and contribute to economic development.

Mr Muyangwa says the product is designed to provide both the informal and formal sectors with another avenue for saving money and securing their future.

Speaking in an interview with the media, he said the product has no limitations on how much an individual can save, adding that people can save any amount at any given time.

‘’NAPSA is for everyone, both the informal and formal sectors, and we want to appeal to every individual to take advantage of this product and grow their wealth,” he said.

Meanwhile, a fourth-year student at the University of Zambia (UNZA), Natasha Mpashi, has urged her fellow students and the youth at large to take advantage of the new product and start saving for the future.

Ms Mpashi said young people can start saving now to prepare for their future endeavors.

She said the savings could help them venture into economic activities and enhance their livelihoods.

Ms Mpashi further said the product provides people in the informal sector, such as marketeers and other traders, an opportunity to save part of the income they generate.

“This product is very attractive because it caters for both the formal and informal sectors,” she said.

World.title: Tongue-tie cutting Procedure kills Chilanga baby
World.content:
The Zambia Police Service is investigating a case of manslaughter involving the death of a one-year-old child.

Police Spokesperson, Godfrey Chilabi says Clifford Muleya died following an alleged tongue-tie cutting procedure in Chilanga district.

Mr Chilabi explained that preliminary investigations indicate that on September 25, 2026, around 17:00 hours, the child was taken by his mother, Loveness Ngandu, aged 27, to the house of Ms Enn Pitrosi, aged 98, in Chipapa area of Chilanga.

He stated that this was after the mother suspected that the child had a tongue-tie condition, locally known as “akalimba.”

The Spokesperson said the suspected tongue-tie was allegedly cut by Ms Enn Pitrosi at her house and it is further alleged that she used a finger during the procedure, resulting in an injury inside the child’s mouth and subsequent bleeding.

He explained that the child later became weak and was rushed to Kazionele Clinic, where he was pronounced dead upon arrival.

He said the matter was reported to Chilanga Police Station around 18:00 hours on September 25, 2026 and the police officers visited and inspected the scene.

Mr Chilabi explained that the body of the deceased was subsequently taken to the University Teaching Hospital Mortuary, where it is currently lying pending a postmortem examination.

He explained that Ms Pitrosi has been detained in police custody, and a warn-and-caution statement has been recorded from her as investigations into the matter continue.

“The Zambia Police Service advises members of the public, particularly parents and guardians, to seek professional medical care from qualified healthcare practitioners whenever children require medical attention and avoid allowing unqualified persons to perform medical procedures,” he emphasised.

He explained that the advice follows a similar incident recorded in Chingola on September 22, 2026, in which an eight-month-old child died following an alleged tongue-tie cutting procedure.

World.title: Government calls for increased private sector investment
World.content:
Government has called for increased private sector investment in Northern Province.

Ministry of Tourism Permanent Secretary, Evans Muhanga says this will help unlock the region’s tourism potential and spread economic benefits of the industry to communities across Zambia.

Speaking during the 2026 World Tourism Day commemoration in Kasama, Mr Muhanga observed that the Northern Province possesses a rich combination of natural, cultural, and historical attractions that can make significant contributions to Zambia’s economy.

“Investors should look beyond Zambia’s traditional tourism destinations and explore emerging areas such as Northern Province, where opportunities exist in accommodation, transport, cultural experiences, adventure tourism, conference facilities, culinary tourism and other innovative tourism products,” he said.

He added that as Zambia seeks to increase international tourist arrivals and achieve its long-term target of five million international tourists by 2031, the northern circuit is key.

Mr Muhanga also urged investors to consider opportunities presented by the province’s cultural heritage, traditional ceremonies, historical sites, wildlife and unique tourism experiences to invest in tourism.

He encouraged the use of digital technology and artificial intelligence stating that the two innovations could complement these investments by improving destination marketing, visitor information, market intelligence and the way tourism products are presented to potential visitors.

He however, stressed the need for tourism development and that natural resources must remain environmentally responsible and culturally respectful and protected for future generations.

And Northern Province Acting Permanent Secretary, Beauty Undi-Phiri has called for increased use of technology and innovation in promoting tourism.

Ms Undi-Phiri who was being represented by Northern Province Assistant Secretary, Jordan Mwenya said the 2026 World Tourism Day theme, “Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism,” is particularly relevant to Northern Province as it gives a rich tourism potential.

“The province is endowed with a variety of attractions, including waterfalls, Lake Tanganyika, rich cultural heritage, rock art, wildlife, and other tourism sites, there is need therefore to use new technologies in publishing what the Province has in the tourism sector,” she said.

She added that embracing digital technology and innovation will help showcase the province’s tourism assets.

“Embracing digital technology and innovation will help to connect the province’s tourism assets to global markets, create opportunities for local communities, and promote sustainable tourism,” she added.

She has further reaffirmed the Northern Provincial Administration’s commitment to working with the Ministry of Tourism and other stakeholders to unlock the full potential of the tourism sector.

And Ministry of Tourism, Director Tourism who is also the Chairperson for World Tourism day Organising Committee, Andrew Bwalya observed that there is a need for the tourism sector to embrace and utilise artificial intelligence to improve efficiency.

Dr Bwalya said adopting AI can help the sector enhance tourist experiences, promote destinations more effectively and remain competitive in the rapidly changing global tourism industry.

World.title: Lusaka DC unveils Disaster Risk Reduction Plans
World.content:
Lusaka District Commissioner, Rosa Kayuni says there is need for concerted efforts from all the stakeholders in the district to plan on how the negative effects of the anticipated El-nino can be reduced.

Ms Kayuni noted that the climate information on the national seasonal outlook for 2026/2027 rain season is critical for planning and preparedness for the district.

She was speaking during the District Disaster Risk Reduction Planning (DRRP) meeting in Lusaka.

‘’The information provided is critical for planning and preparedness for our district and therefore, we should use the climate information to strengthen preparedness and protect lives and livelihoods rather than wait for disaster to occur,” she said.

Ms Kayuni lamented that the district had been experiencing serious disasters in the previous years, which were mainly floods and epidemics.

She said it was the duty of the DDMC members to carry out interventions before, during and after a disaster.

The District Commissioner said the departmental disaster risk reduction plans being unveiled must endeavor to prevent, lessen disaster impact, restore livelihoods and enhance resilience among the affected communities.

Lusaka Integrated Solid Waste Management Company, Solid Waste Collecting Officer, Peula Makeleta said her organisation had lined up a program to collect solid waste in the city.

Ms Peula said her organisation had engaged 24 franchise contractors that help to collect waste from markets, households and business premises.

She further said 100 community-based enterprises were also engaged to manage waste in the Peri-urban areas.

“We collect waste from the markets and accumulate points,” she said.

Meanwhile, Senior Agricultural officer, Elizabeth Kabwe said her department had put in place measures to strengthen the early warning system to help prepare the farmers for the negative impacts of the El-nino.

Ms Kabwe added that promotion of drought tolerant seed variety and crops is among the programmes being undertaken by her department.

“We are encouraging farmers to grow early to medium maturing crop varieties during this coming farming season to cope with the projected El-nino weather patterns,” she said.

World.title: Chipata City Council football club boasts of five new signings
World.content:
Chipata City Council Football Club has bolstered its squad with five new signings ahead of the 2026/27 football season.

The new arrivals are strikers Healings Sinyinza and Morgan Botha, both from Airport Warriors, defender Paul Kapendo from Shooting Stars, midfielder Felix Phiri, popularly known as Neymar, from Mika FC, and right-back Emmanuel Mwila Malata from Immig FC in Central Province.

Chipata City Council FC Media officer, Taonga Mofya said the new players are expected to add depth and competition to the squad.

“The new additions will add depth, competition and fresh energy to the squad as we prepare for the challenges of the new season,” she said.

Mofya said the club was confident that the five players would make a meaningful contribution to the team’s objectives during the 2026/27 season.

She said Sinyinza and Botha are expected to strengthen the club’s attacking options, while Kapendo will provide additional strength and experience in defence.

The Club Media officer said Phiri will add another option in midfield, with Malata strengthening the right-back position.

Mofya welcomed the five players to the Chipata City Council FC family and wished them success as they begin their new chapter with the club.
